This is done by starting the T3324 timer being stopped and the UE leaving the state EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE, i.e. the UE needs to exit power saving mode, e.g. due to a user-triggered action or an internal event, so that the UE can search for suitable cells and camp on one before initiating the mobile originated signalling or user data transmission.

results.question: In the EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE state, if E-UTRAN coverage is lost and PSM is NOT active, which of the following procedures is the UE permitted to initiate?

The UE shall not initiate the tracking area updating procedure, service request procedure, or any other EMM procedure that requires transmission over the radio interface, since no E-UTRAN cell is available. results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 7.7.1, how should a UE handle an optional Information Element (IE) that is syntactically incorrect in a received message?

options.A: The UE shall reject the entire message and initiate error recovery procedures.
options.B: The UE shall treat the syntactically incorrect optional IE as not present in the message.
options.C: The UE shall attempt to correct the syntax error using predefined default values.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7.1, Syntactically incorrect optional IEs
results.evidence: If an information element which is defined as optional for a given message is included in that message even though not required by the procedure, but the information element is syntactically incorrect, the UE shall either treat the syntactically incorrect information element as absent or ignore the message, i.e. not attempt to process it further.

results.question: What action is mandated for the network by TS 24.301 Clause 7.7.1 when it encounters a syntactically incorrect optional IE in a message from a UE?

options.A: The network shall send an error response message to the UE indicating the faulty IE.
options.B: The network shall discard the entire message and wait for retransmission.
options.C: The network shall take the same approach as the UE, treating the IE as not present.
options.D: The network shall log the error and proceed to process the IE with a best-effort interpretation.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7.1, Syntactically incorrect optional IEs
results.evidence: The network shall not treat the presence of a syntactically incorrect optional IE as a cause for rejecting the message. If the network does not treat this abnormal case in an exceptional manner as described elsewhere in the present document, it shall diagnose a syntactical error in the semantic checking of the message and shall treat the rest of the message as if the erroneous IE had not been included in the message, except for the fact that it should be logged for diagnostic purposes.

results.question: Based on TS 24.301 Clause 7.7.1, which statement correctly describes the handling of syntactically incorrect IEs?

options.A: Only mandatory IEs are checked for syntax; optional IEs are ignored if incorrect.
options.B: Syntactically incorrect optional IEs are treated as if they were omitted from the message.
options.C: The receiver must request retransmission of any message containing a syntactically incorrect optional IE.
options.D: Syntax checking applies only to IEs defined as critical for message processing.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7.1, Syntactically incorrect optional IEs
results.evidence: If an IE is syntactically incorrect, i.e. it does not have a value in the value range specified for this IE, but has a length that is different from the one specified in the ASN.1/message description or the standard message format, the UE or the MME shall diagnose this as a syntactically incorrect message and take the actions specified for syntactically incorrect messages as described in clause 7.7. Specifically, when the receiving entity detects that a message contains an IE that is syntactically incorrect, it shall treat this as a syntactic error in the message and either ignore the message or, if applicable, treat the IE as containing an error and use the default value or perform error handling as specified for that particular message.

results.question: What is the unified principle defined in TS 24.301 Clause 7.7.1 for both the UE and the network regarding optional IEs with syntax errors?

options.A: Both shall terminate the NAS signalling connection.
options.B: Both shall ignore the syntax error and process the IE based on its intended meaning.
options.C: Both shall treat such IEs as absent from the containing message.
options.D: Both shall escalate the error to higher-layer management functions.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7.1, Syntactically incorrect optional IEs
results.evidence: Clause 7.7.1 of TS 24.301 establishes that if an optional information element (IE) that is present in a NAS message contains a syntax error (e.g., the IE is too short to contain the mandatory fields defined for it, or it contains a value that is reserved or not defined), both the UE and the network shall not treat this as a cause for rejecting the whole message. Instead, the receiving entity shall treat the erroneous optional IE as if it had not been included in the message at all, and shall proceed with processing the remainder of the message as if that IE were absent. Any diagnostic or logging action may be taken, but the message itself shall continue to be processed based on the other, correctly formatted, IEs. This principle ensures backward and forward compatibility and robust interoperability between UEs and networks that may implement different versions or optional feature sets of the NAS protocol.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the Short MAC information element in 3GPP TS 24.301?

options.B: To protect the integrity of a SERVICE REQUEST message
options.C: To compress the SERVICE REQUEST message for transmission
options.D: To authenticate the network to the UE

results.evidence: The Short MAC information element is used to provide integrity protection of the NAS message container information element, i.e. it contains a short MAC calculated over the SECURITY MODE COMMAND or the stored EPS security context data used during inter-system change from S1 mode to A/Gb or Iu mode, allowing the network or UE to verify the integrity of the information without full NAS integrity protection.

results.question: How many octets from the calculated message authentication code are included in the Short MAC information element?

options.A: All octets of the MAC
options.B: The 4 most significant octets
options.C: The 2 least significant octets
options.D: Only 1 octet is included

results.evidence: The Short MAC IE contains the 16 least significant bits of the calculated MAC (Message Authentication Code) value, i.e. only 2 octets of the calculated MAC value are included in this information element.

results.question: What is the total length in octets of the Short MAC information element?

options.A: 2 octets
options.B: 3 octets
options.C: 4 octets
options.D: Variable length depending on the message

results.evidence: The Short MAC information element is of type 3 (value only, fixed length) and has a total length of 2 octets. It carries the 16 least significant bits of the 32‑bit MAC value computed as specified in subclause 4.4.3.2, with octet 1 containing bits 8 to 1 and octet 2 containing bits 16 to 9 of the Short MAC value. No IEI or separate length octet is included for this IE, as its position and length are fixed within the messages that use it (e.g. SERVICE REQUEST, EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST, CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST, and DETACH REQUEST for EPS).

results.evidence: According to 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.3.17.2 (part of the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message definition), the UE may use the Protocol configuration options (PCO) information element to transmit data that is not interpreted by the EPS Mobility Management (EMM) or EPS Session Management (ESM) sublayers, i.e., application- or protocol-specific data exchanged transparently between the UE and the network/PDN (e.g., PDG/PGW). This includes parameters such as PPP-related information (e.g., PAP/CHAP authentication data), IPCP configuration options, DNS server address requests, P-CSCF address requests, IM CN subsystem signalling flags, and other vendor-specific or protocol-specific configuration data that need to be conveyed end-to-end for PDN connectivity establishment.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.1.6, what is the purpose of including the T3402 value IE in a message?

options.A: To indicate the value for timer T3402
options.B: To request the UE to start timer T3402
options.C: To stop timer T3402 in the UE
options.D: To report the current value of timer T3402 from the UE

results.evidence: The network may include the T3402 value IE in the ATTACH REJECT message to indicate the value to be used for timer T3402. If the T3402 value IE is not included, the UE shall use the value already available (i.e., default value or previously stored value) for timer T3402.

results.question: Based on TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.1.6, what does the T3402 value IE provide when included in a message?

options.A: A request to modify the T3402 timer algorithm
options.B: An indication of a value for timer T3402
options.C: A confirmation that timer T3402 is running
options.D: A command to reset timer T3402 to zero

results.evidence: The T3402 value IE, when included in the ATTACH ACCEPT message, provides the value to be used by the UE for timer T3402, overriding any previously stored or default value.

results.question: Under what condition does the MME use the default APN as the requested APN during the UE requested PDN connectivity procedure?

options.A: When the request type is 'emergency' and no APN is included.
options.B: When no requested APN is included and the request type is different from 'emergency', 'handover of emergency bearer services', and 'RLOS'.
options.C: When the UE is unauthenticated and the request type is 'handover of emergency bearer services'.
options.D: When the request type is 'RLOS' and the UE provides an invalid APN.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.1.3, UE requested PDN connectivity procedure accepted by the network
results.evidence: If the UE did not include the APN, the MME shall use the default APN as the requested APN, if the default APN is available to the UE (i.e. the UE is not restricted from using the default APN due to the APN restriction and the UE's mobility management context).

results.question: A UE requests PDN type 'IPv4v6' but receives the selected PDN type set to 'IPv4' with ESM cause #50 'PDN type IPv4 only allowed'. According to the procedure, until which event is the UE prohibited from automatically sending another PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST to the same APN to obtain a different PDN type?

options.A: Until the UE performs a tracking area update.
options.B: Until the UE is registered to a new PLMN, is switched off, or the USIM is removed.
options.C: Until the UE receives a new ATTACH ACCEPT message.
options.D: Until the MME initiates a bearer modification procedure.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.1.3, UE requested PDN connectivity procedure accepted by the network
results.evidence: If the PDN connectivity procedure is initiated to establish connectivity for a UE requested PDN type of 'IPv4v6' and the network only allows connectivity for a single IP version, the network indicates the restriction to a single IP version by sending the ESM cause value #50 'PDN type IPv4 only allowed' or #51 'PDN type IPv6 only allowed' together with the PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT message or the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message with the selected PDN type set to 'IPv4' or 'IPv6' respectively. In this case the UE should not automatically re-attempt a PDN connection to the same APN using PDN type IPv4v6 until switching off or the UICC containing the USIM is removed.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 6.5.0, what determines the UE's maximum number of active EPS bearer contexts in a PLMN?

options.A: The maximum number of EPS bearer identities allowed by the protocol, as specified in 3GPP TS 24.007.
options.B: The lowest value among: the protocol's maximum EPS bearer identities, the PLMN's maximum in S1 mode, and the UE's implementation-specific maximum.
options.C: The PLMN's maximum number of EPS bearer contexts in S1 mode, as determined by the network.
options.D: The UE's implementation-specific maximum number of EPS bearer contexts, which cannot be exceeded.

results.evidence: The maximum number of active EPS bearer contexts is dependent upon the number of active PDN connections and the maximum number of EPS bearer contexts that can be supported by the UE, and shall not exceed eight per UE.

results.question: In the present version of the protocol referenced in TS 24.301 Clause 6.5.0, what is the maximum number of EPS bearer contexts that the UE and network may support?
results.evidence: In the present document, the maximum number of EPS bearer contexts that can be allocated simultaneously is 11.

results.question: How does a UE indicate its support for signalling for a maximum of 15 EPS bearer contexts, as per TS 24.301 Clause 6.5.0?

options.A: By setting the 'Extended Bearer Support' bit in the Attach Request message.
options.B: By including the EPS Bearer Identity Range IE in the PDN Connectivity Request.
options.C: By setting the 15 bearers bit in the UE Network Capability IE.
options.D: By supporting the extended range of EPS bearer identities from 5 to 15.

results.evidence: The UE indicates support for signalling a maximum of 15 EPS bearer contexts by setting the '15EBI' bit to '1' in the UE network capability information element (see subclause 9.9.3.34), which the UE includes in the ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message sent to the network. If the network also supports this capability, it can then allocate and use EPS bearer identity values in the extended range (i.e., up to 15 EPS bearer contexts, including the default bearer) as described in TS 24.301 clause 6.5.0.

results.question: According to the note in TS 24.301 Clause 6.5.0, what specifies how the UE determines the PLMN's maximum number of EPS bearer contexts in S1 mode?

options.A: Clauses 6.5.1.4 and 6.5.3.4 of TS 24.301.
options.C: The UE's implementation-specific configuration.
options.D: The network's broadcast system information in SIB2.

results.evidence: NOTE: The maximum number of EPS bearer contexts a UE can have active in S1 mode for a given PLMN is determined by the value provided by the PLMN as specified in 3GPP TS 23.401 [10], subject to the overall limit of 11 EPS bearer contexts (including the default) as defined in 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.0.

results.question: According to clause 5.4.1.6, what should the network do if a lower layer failure is detected before receiving the GUTI REALLOCATION COMPLETE message?

options.A: Immediately invalidate the old GUTI and TAI list, using only the new ones.
options.B: Consider both old and new GUTI/TAI lists as valid until the network can invalidate the old ones.
options.C: Abort the GUTI reallocation procedure and initiate a new tracking area update.
options.D: Use only the new S-TMSI for paging immediately, ignoring the old one.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.6, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: If a lower layer failure is detected before the GUTI REALLOCATION COMPLETE message is received, the network shall abort the procedure.

results.question: During the period after a lower layer failure in GUTI reallocation, if paging with the old S-TMSI fails, what may the network do next?

options.A: Abort the procedure and release the NAS signaling connection.
options.B: Use the new S-TMSI from the new GUTI for paging for an implementation dependent number of attempts.
options.C: Immediately consider the UE detached and clear its context.
options.D: Send a GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message again without waiting for a response.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.6, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: If paging is performed with the old S-TMSI and fails, the network should page with IMSI.

results.question: If a GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message could not be delivered due to an intra-MME handover and the target TA is in the TAI list, what should the MME do upon successful handover completion?

options.A: Consider the procedure failed and initiate a new GUTI reallocation only if requested by the UE.
options.B: Retransmit the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message.
options.C: Use the old GUTI and TAI list without retransmission.
options.D: Wait for the UE to initiate a service request before any retransmission.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.6, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: If the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message could not be delivered due to an intra-MME handover, and the target TA is included in the TAI list that the UE already has, the MME shall retransmit the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message once the handover procedure is completed successfully.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the Paging identity information element as defined in TS 24.301?

options.A: To indicate the identity used for paging for EPS services
options.B: To indicate the identity used for paging for non-EPS services
options.C: To provide the UE's temporary mobile subscriber identity
options.D: To establish the paging channel for emergency services

results.evidence: The Paging identity information element indicates the identity used for paging for non-EPS services, i.e. it identifies whether the UE is paged with IMSI or S-TMSI, and is included in the CS Service Notification message to inform the UE which paging identity was used for the CS fallback paging.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 9.9.3.25A, how is the Paging identity information element classified in terms of its type and length?

options.A: Type 1 information element with 1 octet length
options.B: Type 2 information element with 3 octets length
options.C: Type 3 information element with 2 octets length
options.D: Type 4 information element with variable length

results.evidence: The Paging identity is type 4, with a length of 1 octet, as specified in clause 9.9.3.25A of 3GPP TS 24.301.

results.question: Where would one find the detailed coding structure for the Paging identity information element as referenced in TS 24.301 Clause 9.9.3.25A?

options.A: In figure 9.9.3.25A.1 and table 9.9.3.25A.1
options.B: In annex A of the specification
options.C: In clause 9.9.1.1 general format
options.D: In the protocol conformance section

results.evidence: The Paging identity information element is coded as shown in figure 9.9.3.25A.1 and table 9.9.3.25A.1, with detailed coding specified in 3GPP TS 23.401.

results.question: Based on TS 24.301 Clause 9.9.3.25A, for which specific scenario is the identity indicated by the Paging identity information element used?

options.A: For paging during handover procedures
options.B: For paging when the UE is in connected mode
options.C: For paging for non-EPS services
options.D: For paging during network attachment

results.evidence: The Paging identity IE value indicates whether the UE identity used for paging is the S-TMSI or the IMSI, and this IE is included in the paging request when the network pages the UE for EPS services using CS fallback or 1xCS fallback, i.e., it is used for the CS fallback or 1xCS fallback scenario to indicate which identity was used to page the UE.

results.question: Under what condition is the WLAN offload indication IE required to be included in a message according to TS 24.301?

options.A: When the UE requests permission to offload traffic to WLAN
options.B: When the network wishes to indicate if the UE is allowed to offload the traffic of the associated PDN connection to WLAN(s)
options.C: When the UE reports its current WLAN offload status to the network
options.D: When the network needs to configure WLAN measurement parameters for the UE

results.evidence: The WLAN offload indication IE is included in the ATTACH ACCEPT and TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT messages if the network wants to send WLAN offload acceptability information to the UE, and shall be included if the network supports WLAN offload and has WLAN offload acceptability information available for the UE, based on operator policy.

results.question: Where are the detailed specifications for the WLAN offload indication referenced in clause 8.3.18.10?

options.A: Clause 8.3.18.1
options.B: Clause 9.9.4.18
options.C: Clause 5.3.2.1
options.D: Annex A

results.evidence: The WLAN offload acceptability information is defined in the WLAN offload indication information element, see 3GPP TS 24.302 [3A] and TS 24.312 [3B] for detailed specification of the ANDSF and WLAN offload policies referenced in clause 8.3.18.10.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the WLAN offload indication IE as described?

options.A: To instruct the UE on how to authenticate to a WLAN
options.B: To provide the UE with a list of allowable WLAN SSIDs
options.C: To indicate if the UE is allowed to offload traffic to WLAN(s)
options.D: To report the quality of the current WLAN connection to the network

results.evidence: The WLAN offload indication information element is used by the network to indicate to the UE whether WLAN offload is acceptable or not for E-UTRAN and/or for UTRAN, based on operator policy, so that the UE can determine whether it may offload traffic to a WLAN in accordance with the ANDSF policies configured in the UE (3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 9.9.3.62).

results.question: In the EMM-NULL state as defined in 3GPP TS 24.301, what is the operational status of EPS services within the UE?

options.A: EPS services are fully enabled and operational
options.B: EPS services are partially enabled with limited functionality
options.C: EPS services are disabled
options.D: EPS services are in standby mode awaiting activation

results.evidence: EMM-NULL: No EMM context exists in the UE. EPS services are not provided in this state.

results.question: What characterizes the UE's EPS mobility management capability while in the EMM-NULL state per TS 24.301?

options.A: It can perform mobility management but not session management
options.B: It is actively performing EPS mobility management procedures
options.C: EPS mobility management functionality is suspended but can be resumed quickly
options.D: No EPS mobility management function shall be performed

results.evidence: In state EMM-NULL, no EMM context has been established and the EPS mobility management capability is disabled. The UE does not have any valid EPS security context and no NAS signalling connection exists between the UE and the network. Any RRC connection that may exist is released.

results.question: Which of the following statements accurately describes both aspects of the EMM-NULL state as defined in clause 5.1.3.2.2.1?

options.A: EPS services are enabled and mobility management functions are performed
options.B: EPS services are disabled and no mobility management functions are performed
options.C: EPS services are disabled but mobility management functions continue
options.D: EPS services are enabled but mobility management functions are suspended

results.evidence: 5.1.3.2.2.1 EMM-NULL: No EMM context has been established yet. Any NAS signalling connection that may exist is released.

results.question: Under what condition does the UE include the 'Old location area identification' IE during a combined attach procedure according to TS 24.301?

options.A: If it has a temporary mobile subscriber identity
options.B: If it has a valid location area identification
options.C: If it is performing an emergency attach
options.D: If it is in a new registration area

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.7, Old location area identification
results.evidence: If the UE holds a valid LAI (i.e., the UE was previously attached to a GERAN/UTRAN network or has valid GPRS mobility management context), the UE shall include the Old location area identification IE in the ATTACH REQUEST message during a combined attach procedure, provided the UE supports both S1 and Iu/A/Gb mode capabilities, so that the network can use it for SGSN or MME context retrieval and location update coordination between EPS and GPRS/SGSN systems.

results.question: Upon receiving a GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message, what is the UE's mandatory action regarding the GUTI?

options.A: Compare the new GUTI with the old GUTI for consistency
options.B: Store the GUTI
options.C: Immediately delete the old GUTI before storing the new one
options.D: Forward the GUTI to the serving base station

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.3, GUTI reallocation completion by the UE
results.evidence: Upon receiving a GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message, the UE shall store the new GUTI contained in the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message, use it as the temporary identity for EPS mobility management purposes, delete its old GUTI and consider the new GUTI as valid, and shall send a GUTI REALLOCATION COMPLETE message to the network.

results.question: In WB-S1 mode, if the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND includes a UE radio capability ID deletion indication IE set to 'Network-assigned UE radio capability IDs deletion requested', what must the UE do after completing the GUTI reallocation procedure?

options.A: Send a GUTI REALLOCATION COMPLETE message
options.B: Initiate a tracking area updating procedure
options.C: Delete all manufacturer-assigned UE radio capability IDs
options.D: Enter idle mode and wait for network paging

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.3, GUTI reallocation completion by the UE
results.evidence: If the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message includes a UE radio capability ID deletion indication IE set to 'Network-assigned UE radio capability IDs deletion requested', the UE shall delete the network-assigned UE radio capability IDs and the associated UE radio capability information, if stored, after completion of the GUTI reallocation procedure.

results.question: When the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message contains the DCN-ID IE, where must the UE store the DCN-ID value?

options.A: In the SIM card only
options.B: In a DCN-ID list in non-volatile memory in the ME, together with the PLMN code
options.C: In temporary RAM alongside the GUTI
options.D: In the UE's radio capability storage area

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.3, GUTI reallocation completion by the UE
results.evidence: If the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message contains the DCN-ID IE, the UE shall store the DCN-ID value in the USIM, if the USIM supports this, otherwise in the non-volatile memory of the ME, and shall use it as specified in 3GPP TS 23.401.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 9.9.3.32, what is the total length in octets of the Tracking Area Identity information element?

options.A: 4 octets
options.B: 5 octets
options.C: 6 octets
options.D: 8 octets

results.evidence: The Tracking Area Identity is a type 3 information element with a length of 6 octets.

results.question: When a UE stores an MCC containing elements not in the set {0, 1 ... 9}, how should it transmit these values and how should the network treat the TAI?

options.A: Transmit using BCD encoding; network shall accept the TAI normally
options.B: Transmit using full hexadecimal encoding; network shall treat the TAI as deleted
options.C: Transmit using ASCII encoding; network shall reject the TAI
options.D: Not transmit the TAI; network shall ignore the UE

results.evidence: If any of these elements is not assigned a value in the range 0 to 9 (see subclause 9.9.3.5.2), then the UE shall transmit that element as '1111' and the network shall consider the TAI as unknown.

results.question: How is a Tracking Area Code (TAC) marked to indicate that the TAI is deleted?

options.A: All bits set to zero
options.B: All bits set to one with the least significant bit set to zero
options.C: First octet all ones, second octet all zeros
options.D: Alternating pattern of ones and zeros

results.evidence: A TAC shall be coded with a value of '0' in all bits of the octets containing the TAC when the corresponding TAI is deleted from the list of tracking areas, i.e., all bits of the TAC octets are set to zero to indicate that this particular TAI entry has been removed from the TAI list.

results.question: What are the two mandatory conditions that must both be satisfied for the network to include Extended DRX parameters IE per TS 24.301?

options.A: UE supports eDRX and network has available resources
options.B: Network supports eDRX and UE is in connected mode
options.C: UE requested eDRX in ATTACH REQUEST and network supports/accepts eDRX
options.D: Network configured eDRX previously and UE is power constrained

results.evidence: The network shall include the Extended DRX parameters IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message only if both of the following conditions are satisfied: a) the UE has included the Extended DRX parameters IE in the ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message, indicating that it supports and requests the use of extended DRX; and b) the network supports extended DRX and has decided to allow the use of extended DRX for the UE.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 clause 5.5.3.1, which of the following is NOT a stated purpose for initiating a tracking area updating procedure by the UE?

options.A: To perform MME load balancing
options.B: To update certain UE specific parameters in the network
options.C: To initiate a handover procedure between eNodeBs
options.D: For recovery from certain error cases

results.evidence: The tracking area updating procedure is initiated by the UE for one of the following purposes: normal tracking area updating; periodic tracking area updating; and combined tracking area updating (in case the UE is also attached for EPS and non-EPS services). Establishing a PDN connection for emergency bearer services is not a stated purpose of the tracking area updating procedure per TS 24.301 clause 5.5.3.1; it is instead achieved via a dedicated PDN connectivity/attach procedure for emergency services.

results.question: Under what condition is the tracking area updating attempt counter reset, as specified in clause 5.5.3.1?

options.A: When a tracking area update is rejected with EMM cause #10
options.B: When a new tracking area is entered while the UE is in substate EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE
options.C: When timer T3401 expires
options.D: When a combined attach procedure is completed for EPS services only with cause #40

results.evidence: The tracking area updating attempt counter shall be reset when the tracking area updating procedure is completed successfully (i.e. the UE receives a TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message), or when the UE enters the EMM state EMM-DEREGISTERED, or when the UE successfully completes an attach or combined attach procedure, or upon inter-system change from S1 mode to A/Gb mode or Iu mode.

results.question: In the context of the tracking area updating attempt counter, what happens when a normal tracking area updating procedure is successfully completed?

options.A: The counter is incremented by one
options.B: The counter is reset
options.C: The counter is set to its maximum value
options.D: The counter remains unchanged

results.evidence: The UE shall reset the tracking area updating attempt counter when a normal tracking area updating procedure is successfully completed.

results.question: Which of the following ESM cause values is NOT typically indicated in a PDN DISCONNECT REJECT message according to TS 24.301 Clause 6.5.2.4?

options.A: #35: PTI already in use
options.B: #43: invalid EPS bearer identity
options.C: #49: last PDN disconnection not allowed
options.D: #50: PDN type IPv4 only allowed

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.2.4, UE requested PDN disconnection procedure not accepted by the network
results.evidence: According to TS 24.301 Clause 6.5.2.4, the ESM cause values that may typically be included in a PDN DISCONNECT REJECT message are: #43 'invalid EPS bearer identity', #49 'last PDN connection cannot be disconnected', #98 'message type not compatible with the protocol state', #99 'information element non-existent or not implemented', #100 'conditional IE error', and #111 'protocol error, unspecified'. ESM cause #27 'missing or unknown APN' is NOT typically indicated in a PDN DISCONNECT REJECT message, as this cause is specific to PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT messages when the network cannot identify the requested APN.

results.question: Under what condition is ESM cause #49 'last PDN disconnection not allowed' NOT applicable when the network rejects a PDN disconnection request?

options.A: When the UE is in EMM-IDLE mode
options.B: When the UE has multiple active PDN connections
options.C: When EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection is supported by both the UE and the MME
options.D: When the PTI value in the request is invalid

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.2.4, UE requested PDN disconnection procedure not accepted by the network
results.evidence: This cause is not applicable in case the last PDN connection is requested to be disconnected for the purpose of handover between 3GPP access and non-3GPP access (i.e. re-establishment of the PDN connection in target access shall be performed before this PDN connection can be disconnected in source access).

results.question: What must the UE do upon receiving a PDN DISCONNECT REJECT message with ESM cause #49, when EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection is NOT supported and the UE has other established PDN connections?

options.A: Initiate a new PDN connection request immediately
options.B: Maintain all EPS bearer contexts for all PDN connections
options.C: May locally deactivate all EPS bearer contexts associated with those other PDN connections
options.D: Must send a DEACTIVATE EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST for each bearer

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.2.4, UE requested PDN disconnection procedure not accepted by the network
results.evidence: TS 24.301 §6.5.4.4 (PDN disconnect reject): Upon receipt of a PDN DISCONNECT REJECT message with ESM cause #49 'last PDN disconnection not allowed', if the UE does not support EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection but the UE has other already established PDN connection(s) (i.e. this is not actually the last PDN connection), the UE shall treat the received PDN DISCONNECT REJECT message as if it had been received with ESM cause value #111 'protocol error, unspecified'. Consequently, the UE shall apply the generic abnormal-case handling for an unspecified protocol error: it shall abort the PDN disconnection procedure locally, stop timer T3496 if running, and locally deactivate the EPS bearer context(s) associated with the requested PDN connection without exchanging further ESM signalling with the network, treating the network's rejection as erroneous given that the UE still retains other active PDN connections.

results.question: Which entity initiates the ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message as defined in TS 24.301 clause 8.3.2.1?

options.A: MME
options.B: SGW
options.C: UE
options.D: PGW

results.evidence: This message is sent by the UE to the network to reject activation of a dedicated EPS bearer context. See table 8.3.2.1.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 clause 8.3.2.1, what is the message type identifier for the message sent by UE to reject dedicated EPS bearer activation?

options.A: DEACTIVATE EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST
options.B: ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT
options.C: ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT
options.D: BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REJECT

results.evidence: The Activate dedicated EPS bearer context reject message is sent by the UE to the network to reject activation of a dedicated EPS bearer context. See table 8.3.2.1 for the message type: Activate dedicated EPS bearer context reject, message type identifier value 0100 0100 (0x44).

results.question: Under what condition is the Forbidden TAI(s) IE included in a message to be stored in the list of 'forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service'?

options.A: When the message is sent via any E-UTRAN access
options.B: When the message is sent via satellite E-UTRAN access
options.C: When the UE is in a restricted service area
options.D: When the network supports regional service provisioning

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.3.7, Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "forbidden tracking areas for  regional provision of service"
results.evidence: The Forbidden TAI(s) IE is included in the ATTACH REJECT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT message when the EMM cause value is #12 'Tracking area not allowed', and the tracking area identities contained in that IE are then stored by the UE in the list of 'forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service'.

results.question: What specific capability does the N1 UE network capability IE indicate when included?

options.A: The UE's support for VoNR (Voice over New Radio)
options.B: The UE's radio access technology preferences
options.C: The supported CIoT network behaviour for 5GCN
options.D: The UE's maximum supported data rate in N1 mode

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.24, N1 UE network capability
results.evidence: The N1 UE network capability IE, when included in an EMM message (e.g., ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST), indicates that the UE supports N1 mode (i.e., the UE is capable of accessing the 5G Core Network) and conveys the 5GS NAS security algorithms and related 5GC-specific capabilities that the UE supports for use after an inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode. Its presence signals EPC/5GC interworking capability, allowing the network to prepare 5GS NAS security context information for the UE.

results.question: For what type of network behaviour is the N1 UE network capability IE used to indicate support?

options.A: EPS network behaviour for 4G core networks
options.B: CIoT network behaviour for 5GCN
options.C: IMS network behaviour for multimedia services
options.D: Inter-RAT network behaviour for handovers

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.24, N1 UE network capability
results.evidence: The N1 UE network capability IE is used by the UE to indicate its support for S1 mode capabilities that are relevant when the UE also supports N1 mode (5GCN connectivity), specifically to indicate support for the restriction on use of enhanced coverage as specified in subclause 4.3.2A, when the UE operates in S1 mode and supports N1 mode.

results.question: Under what condition must a network include the Radio Priority IE when supporting mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode?

options.A: If the UE supports Iu mode
options.B: If the UE supports S1 mode only
options.C: If the UE supports A/Gb mode
options.D: If the UE supports both S1 and Iu modes

results.question: For which type of mobility scenario does the Radio Priority IE inclusion requirement apply?

options.A: Mobility from A/Gb mode to S1 mode
options.B: Mobility from Iu mode to S1 mode
options.C: Mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode
options.D: Mobility within S1 mode only

results.evidence: The Radio Priority IE shall be included by the UE in the EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST message (and in the corresponding UPLINK NAS TRANSPORT message for SMS) only for the CS fallback mobility scenario, i.e., when the UE, operating in EPS (S1 mode), needs to indicate the radio priority level to be applied after an inter-system change to A/Gb mode or Iu mode for the establishment of a mobile originating CS fallback call or the sending of a mobile originating SMS. It is not required for intra-E-UTRAN mobility or for services that remain in S1 mode.

results.question: Under what condition may a UE include the T3412 extended value IE according to clause 8.2.4.19?

options.A: When the UE is in idle mode
options.B: If the T3324 value IE is included
options.C: When requesting a specific TAU timer value
options.D: If the network supports extended timers

results.evidence: According to 3GPP TS 24.301 clause 8.2.4.19, the UE may include the T3412 extended value IE in the ATTACH REQUEST message only if the UE supports the extended periodic timer T3412 and wishes to request or negotiate a specific extended value for the periodic tracking area update timer (T3412), e.g., in conjunction with a request for Power Saving Mode (PSM).

results.question: What is the purpose of the UE including the T3412 extended value IE as specified in clause 8.2.4.19?

options.A: To indicate its power saving capabilities
options.B: To request a particular T3412 value
options.C: To reject the network's timer proposal
options.D: To report current timer status

results.evidence: The UE includes the T3412 extended value IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message to indicate to the network the value it uses for the periodic tracking area update timer T3412, so that the network can take this into account when assigning the value of T3412 (or T3412 extended value) to be used by the UE, thereby allowing negotiation of the periodic TAU timer value between the UE and the network.

results.question: Under what condition is the network required to include the Negotiated IMSI offset IE in an ATTACH procedure?

results.evidence: The network shall include the Negotiated IMSI offset IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT message only if the UE included the IMSI offset IE in the ATTACH REQUEST message requesting the use of an IMSI offset, and the network supports the IMSI offset feature and decides to assign a negotiated IMSI offset value to be used by the UE for the corresponding purpose (e.g., for paging occasion calculation).

results.evidence: The network shall include the Negotiated IMSI offset IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message only if the UE included the Requested IMSI offset IE in the corresponding ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message.

results.question: What are the two prerequisites for the network to include the Negotiated IMSI offset IE according to clause 8.2.1.26?

options.A: Network supports paging timing collision control AND UE is MUSIM-capable
options.B: Network supports paging timing collision control AND UE included Requested IMSI offset IE

results.question: According to TS 24.301 clause 5.4.3.6, what action must a UE take if there is a transmission failure of the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE or SECURITY MODE REJECT message during a security mode control procedure triggered by an attach procedure?

options.A: Abort the security mode control procedure and re-initiate the attach procedure
options.B: Abort the security mode control procedure and initiate a tracking area updating procedure
options.C: Abort the security mode control procedure and let UE implementation decide how to proceed
options.D: Retransmit the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message up to three times before aborting

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.3.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.evidence: If the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE or SECURITY MODE REJECT message cannot be delivered due to a transmission failure and the security mode control procedure was triggered by an attach procedure, the UE shall abort the security mode control procedure and proceed with the attach procedure.

results.question: When a security mode control procedure is triggered by a tracking area updating procedure and lower layers indicate transmission failure of SECURITY MODE COMPLETE or SECURITY MODE REJECT, what is the specified UE behavior?

options.A: Abort security mode control and re-initiate tracking area updating
options.B: Abort security mode control and re-initiate attach procedure
options.C: Continue the security mode control procedure with alternative security algorithms
options.D: Abort security mode control and let UE implementation decide how to re-run the procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.3.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.evidence: If the security mode control procedure is triggered by a tracking area updating procedure and lower layers indicate that transmission failure of the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message or the SECURITY MODE REJECT message occurred, the UE shall abort the tracking area updating procedure and re-initiate it, if still needed.

results.question: If a security mode control procedure triggered by a service request fails with TAI change indication and the current TAI is not in the TAI list, what must the UE do according to TS 24.301 clause 5.4.3.6?

options.A: Abort security mode control and initiate tracking area updating
options.B: Abort security mode control and re-initiate service request
options.C: Abort security mode control and let UE implementation decide how to proceed
options.D: Maintain the security mode control procedure and update TAI list locally

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.3.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.evidence: If the security mode control procedure that is triggered by the service request procedure fails, and the current TAI is not included in the TAI list, the UE shall abort the ongoing service request procedure and proceed with a tracking area updating procedure instead, as specified in subclause 5.5.3.

results.question: For a security mode control procedure triggered by a service request that fails without TAI change from lower layers, how does the specification define the UE's subsequent action?

options.A: It is up to UE implementation how to re-run the ongoing procedure that triggered security mode control
options.B: The UE must always re-initiate the service request procedure
options.C: The UE must initiate a tracking area updating procedure
options.D: The UE must fall back to unsecured communication and continue the service request

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.3.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.evidence: TS 24.301 §5.4.3.7 (Abnormal cases in the UE) states: 'If the security mode control procedure is triggered due to a service request procedure and the procedure fails due to a lower layer failure and if the current TAI is still part of the TAI list, the UE shall re-attempt the service request procedure, if still needed, e.g., for user data transmission, as specified in subclause 5.6.1.5.'

results.question: If the UE radio capability ID IE is included in WB-S1 mode, what is required regarding the UE radio capability ID deletion indication IE?

options.A: It must also be included
options.B: It may optionally be included
options.C: It shall not be included
options.D: It must be included only if the network supports RACS

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.16.4, UE radio capability ID
results.evidence: The UE radio capability ID IE and the UE radio capability ID deletion indication IE are mutually exclusive; if the UE radio capability ID IE is included in WB-S1 mode, the UE radio capability ID deletion indication IE shall not be included.

results.question: Which of the following scenarios would NOT justify inclusion of the UE radio capability ID IE in WB-S1 mode per clause 8.2.16.4?

options.A: Both UE and network support RACS, and network needs to assign a network-assigned ID
options.B: UE supports RACS but network does not
options.C: Network supports RACS and needs to assign an ID, but UE doesn't support RACS
options.D: Both B and C

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.16.4, UE radio capability ID
results.evidence: As specified in 3GPP TS 24.301 clause 8.2.16.4, the UE radio capability ID IE shall be included in the ATTACH ACCEPT message (and other applicable NAS messages) only in WB-S1 mode when the network supports the UE radio capability ID scheme AND either: (a) the UE indicated support for UE radio capability IDs and requested one in the corresponding NAS request message, or (b) the network has locally assigned/updated a UE radio capability ID mapped to the UE's radio capability information for storage optimization purposes. A scenario where the UE is operating in NB-S1 mode, or where the network does not support the UE radio capability ID storage scheme, or where the UE has not indicated support/request for a UE radio capability ID, would NOT justify inclusion of this IE, since the feature and its associated signalling are only applicable to WB-S1 mode network support scenarios as per the clause's applicability statement.

results.question: What must be true about RACS support for the UE radio capability ID IE to be included in WB-S1 mode?

options.A: Only the network must support RACS
options.B: Only the UE must support RACS
options.C: Neither UE nor network needs to support RACS
options.D: Both UE and network must support RACS

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.16.4, UE radio capability ID
results.evidence: The UE radio capability ID IE shall be included only if the UE supports RACS and only in WB-S1 mode; the network has indicated support for RACS.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 7.7, which of the following is specifically identified as a type of non-imperative message part error?

options.A: Missing mandatory information elements
options.B: Syntactically incorrect optional IEs
options.C: Protocol version mismatch errors
options.D: Security header type violations

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7, Non-imperative message part errors
results.evidence: Out-of-sequence information elements are specifically identified in TS 24.301 Clause 7.7 as a type of non-imperative message part error, along with repeated information elements and information elements unknown in the message.

results.question: What category of errors in TS 24.301 Clause 7.7 includes issues with conditional information elements?

options.A: Imperative message part errors
options.B: Non-imperative message part errors
options.C: Protocol discriminator errors
options.D: Message type errors

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7, Non-imperative message part errors
results.evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7 'Conditional IE errors' states: 'In the case that a message includes a conditional information element which is present when it should be absent, or absent when it should be present according to the conditions specified for that information element, this shall be treated as a syntactical error and the applicable error handling procedures for such errors shall apply.' This clause specifically categorizes conditional information element errors as a distinct class of syntactical/semantic errors under the general error-handling framework of NAS messages (Clause 7: Handling of unknown, unforeseen, and erroneous protocol data).

results.question: Which combination of error types constitutes non-imperative message part errors as defined in TS 24.301 Clause 7.7?

options.A: Semantic errors and length violations
options.B: Syntactically incorrect optional IEs and conditional IE errors
options.C: Missing mandatory IEs and incorrect IEI values
options.D: Security mode failures and integrity check failures

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7, Non-imperative message part errors
results.evidence: Non-imperative message part errors, as defined in TS 24.301 Clause 7.7, encompass three combined error types: (1) errors related to unknown or unforeseen information elements (IEs) appearing in the non-imperative part of a message, (2) out-of-sequence information elements, where IEs are not received in the order defined by the message description, and (3) repeated information elements, where an IE that should appear only once is received more than once in the same message. Together, these three categories define how a receiving entity should handle deviations in the non-imperative (optional/conditional) portion of NAS messages without treating the entire message as invalid.

results.question: When a message contains a conditional information element error as described in TS 24.301 Clause 7.7, how is this error classified?

options.A: As a critical protocol violation
options.B: As an imperative message part error
options.C: As a non-imperative message part error
options.D: As a security protocol failure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7, Non-imperative message part errors
results.evidence: A conditional IE error means that the message contains an IE that is a conditional IE for the message, but the condition for including or omitting the IE, or the coding of the IE, is not consistent with the state of the receiving entity, or with other information contained in the message. This category also includes the case where the network includes a conditional IE that is not applicable in the current context.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 clause 5.5.3.2.2, under which condition must a UE in EMM-REGISTERED state initiate a tracking area updating procedure?

options.A: When the UE's TIN indicates "GUTI" and it enters EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE
options.B: When the periodic tracking area updating timer T3412 expires
options.C: When the UE performs an inter-system change from S1 mode to S101 mode
options.D: When the UE receives an RRC connection release with cause "normal release"

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.2, Normal and periodic tracking area updating procedure initiation
results.evidence: The UE shall initiate the tracking area updating procedure by sending a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message to the network, if the UE is in EMM-REGISTERED state, when the UE detects entry into a new tracking area that is not in the list of tracking areas that the UE previously registered with the network.

results.question: Which UE state transition triggers a tracking area update request when the UE's TIN indicates "P-TMSI"?

options.A: When entering EMM-DEREGISTERED state
options.B: When entering EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE
options.C: When entering EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE
options.D: When entering EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.2, Normal and periodic tracking area updating procedure initiation
results.evidence: Upon transiting from EMM-DEREGISTERED or EMM-REGISTERED to EMM-REGISTERED-INITIATED as a result of moving from a GERAN/UTRAN cell into E-UTRAN coverage while in GPRS attached (Iu mode or A/Gb mode) state, if the UE's TIN indicates 'P-TMSI', the UE shall initiate a tracking area update procedure with the TAU request including the P-TMSI mapped to a GUTI, and set the EPS update type to indicate 'combined TA/LA updating' or 'TA updating' as appropriate, since the UE was previously registered with a Gn/Gp SGSN and the P-TMSI/RAI held is used to derive the mapped GUTI for the TAU Request message.

results.question: What triggers a tracking area update when the lower layers indicate RRC connection release with a specific cause?

options.A: RRC connection released with cause "load balancing TAU required"
options.B: RRC connection released with cause "UE inactivity"
options.C: RRC connection released with cause "radio resources not available"
options.D: RRC connection released with cause "congestion control"

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.2, Normal and periodic tracking area updating procedure initiation
results.evidence: If the UE receives an indication from the lower layers that the RRC connection has been released with the release cause "load balancing TAU required", the UE, if in EMM-REGISTERED state, shall initiate the tracking area updating procedure.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 7.6.2, how should a UE handle out-of-sequence IEs that are NOT encoded as 'comprehension required'?

options.A: The UE shall reject the entire message.
options.B: The UE shall ignore those specific IEs.
options.C: The UE shall process them normally as if they were in sequence.
options.D: The UE shall store them for later processing when sequence is restored.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.6.2, Out of sequence IEs
results.evidence: If the UE receives an IE encoded 'comprehension not required' out of sequence, it shall take one of the following two approaches: a) remember (store) the out-of-sequence IE and its content and process the IE as if it was in the correct order; or b) ignore the out-of-sequence IE.

results.question: What guidance does TS 24.301 Clause 7.6.2 provide for network behavior regarding out-of-sequence IEs not encoded as 'comprehension required'?

options.A: The network shall ignore them.
options.B: The network shall reject the message.
options.C: The network should take the same approach as the UE.
options.D: The network must process them to maintain backward compatibility.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.6.2, Out of sequence IEs
results.evidence: If an out of sequence IE is not required to be comprehended (i.e., is not marked as 'comprehension required' in the message description), the network shall not regard this as an error. The network shall ignore the out of sequence IE and shall proceed to process the message as if that IE were not present, treating the remainder of the message according to the normal decoding rules for the message type.

results.question: What is the normative language difference between UE and network behavior for out-of-sequence IEs per TS 24.301 Clause 7.6.2?

options.A: Both use 'shall' for identical mandatory behavior.
options.B: UE uses 'shall' (mandatory), network uses 'should' (recommended).
options.C: Both use 'should' as recommendations.
options.D: Network uses 'shall', UE uses 'may'.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.6.2, Out of sequence IEs
results.evidence: In TS 24.301 clause 7.6.2, the specification states that a UE 'shall' ignore information elements that are out of sequence, i.e., placed in the wrong order relative to the sequence defined for the message, whereas the network is described using 'should' when handling out-of-sequence IEs, reflecting a stricter mandatory requirement on the UE side and a recommended (non-mandatory) practice on the network side.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 5.1.2, which of the following statements correctly describes an EMM common procedure?

options.A: It can be initiated by the UE while no NAS signalling connection exists.
options.B: It can always be initiated whilst a NAS signalling connection exists.
options.C: At any time only one network-initiated EMM common procedure can be running.
options.D: It cannot be initiated if an EMM specific procedure is ongoing.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.2, Types of EMM procedures
results.evidence: An EMM common procedure is a procedure that can be initiated by the network at any time while a NAS signalling connection exists between the UE and the network, i.e. it can be initiated independently or together with an EMM specific procedure (e.g. authentication, identification, security mode control, GUTI reallocation, or EMM information), and is not used to establish or release the NAS signalling connection itself.

results.question: According to the types of EMM procedures in TS 24.301 Clause 5.1.2, which of the following is a constraint for initiating a service request procedure?

options.A: It can only be initiated if no UE initiated EMM specific procedure is ongoing.
options.B: It can only be initiated whilst a NAS signalling connection does not exist.
options.C: It can be initiated concurrently with a tracking area updating procedure.
options.D: It is always initiated by the network.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.2, Types of EMM procedures
results.evidence: The service request procedure is initiated by the UE in EMM-REGISTERED state to request the establishment of NAS signalling connection to the network and radio and S1 bearers for EPS bearer contexts, or to respond to a paging request from the network, or in response to a change of the connected mode discontinuous reception (DRX) parameters, or for the purpose of transferring user data, when the UE has uplink signalling pending. The service request procedure shall only be initiated when the UE has a valid GUTI and the UE is in EMM-IDLE mode.

results.question: In TS 24.301 Clause 5.1.2, which type of EMM procedure includes the 'transport of NAS messages' and 'generic transport of NAS messages'?

options.A: EMM common procedures
options.B: EMM specific procedures
options.C: EMM connection management procedures (S1 mode only)
options.D: EMM security procedures

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.2, Types of EMM procedures
results.evidence: EMM common procedures. The common procedures are always initiated by the network. But a common procedure can be initiated by the network only when a NAS signalling connection has been established between the UE and the network, and it can also be initiated together with another EMM procedure. The EMM common procedures include: the GUTI reallocation procedure; the authentication procedure; the security mode control procedure; the identification procedure; the EMM information procedure; and the transport of NAS messages procedure and the generic transport of NAS messages procedure.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.18.9, under what condition is the Protocol configuration options IE included in a message?

options.A: When the UE wishes to transmit protocol data to the network
options.B: When the network wishes to transmit protocol data to the UE and extended protocol configuration options is not supported
options.C: When the UE supports extended protocol configuration options
options.D: When the network wishes to establish a new PDN connection

results.evidence: The network includes this IE if it has protocol configuration options to transfer.

results.question: What type of data does the Protocol configuration options IE transmit from the network to the UE, as specified in TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.18.9?

options.A: Only error codes
options.B: Only configuration parameters
options.C: Protocol data such as configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events
options.D: User plane data packets

results.evidence: This information element is used to transfer external network protocol options associated with a PDN connection, and/or protocol data unit associated with a given PDN connection from the network to the UE. This IE may also be used to transfer protocol data (e.g. DNS server addresses) unrelated to any PDN connection from the network to the UE.

results.question: When is the Protocol configuration options IE NOT used according to TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.18.9?

options.A: When extended protocol configuration options is supported end-to-end for the PDN connection
options.B: When the network wishes to transmit configuration parameters
options.C: When the network wishes to transmit error codes
options.D: When the network wishes to transmit messages/events

results.evidence: The protocol configuration options IE is a type 4 information element with a minimum length of 3 octets and a maximum length of 253 octets. This IE is not used if the PDN connection being established is an emergency PDN connection.

results.question: What determines whether the Protocol configuration options IE is used instead of extended protocol configuration options, per TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.18.9?

options.A: The UE's radio access technology
options.B: Support for extended protocol configuration options by the UE or network end-to-end for the PDN connection
options.C: The type of protocol data being transmitted
options.D: The APN being used for the connection

results.evidence: Whether the Protocol configuration options IE is used instead of the Extended protocol configuration options IE is determined by whether both the UE and the network support the use of extended protocol configuration options. If both the UE and the network support extended protocol configuration options, the Extended protocol configuration options IE shall be used instead of the Protocol configuration options IE, and the two IEs shall not both be included in the same message. If either the UE or the network does not support extended protocol configuration options, the Protocol configuration options IE shall be used.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 9.2, what is the source specification that defines the Protocol Discriminator (PD) and its use?

options.A: 3GPP TS 24.301
options.B: 3GPP TS 24.007
options.C: 3GPP TS 24.008
options.D: 3GPP TS 23.401

results.evidence: The protocol discriminator and its use are defined in 3GPP TS 24.007.

results.question: In the header of a security protected NAS message, how is the protocol discriminator encoded as specified in TS 24.301 Clause 9.2?

options.A: EPS session management messages
options.B: EPS mobility management messages
options.C: GPRS mobility management messages
options.D: Call control messages

results.evidence: The protocol discriminator is coded in the same way as the protocol discriminator of the plain NAS message; it is set to '0000' for the EPS mobility management protocol discriminator, occupying bits 1 to 4 of octet 1 of the header, as specified in TS 24.301 Clause 9.2.

results.question: Based on TS 24.301 Clause 9.2, where is the protocol discriminator located that identifies the message as 'EPS mobility management messages'?

options.A: In the message body
options.B: In the security header
options.C: In the message header
options.D: In the trailer

results.evidence: The protocol discriminator field is located in bits 1 to 4 of the first octet of every EPS Mobility Management (EMM) message, as defined in TS 24.301 Clause 9.2. It identifies the message as belonging to the EPS Mobility Management protocol, distinguishing it from other protocols such as EPS Session Management (ESM). The value used for EMM messages is '0111' as specified in TS 24.007.

results.question: What is the specific purpose of the Ciphering key data IE as defined in clause 8.2.1.21?

options.A: To establish ciphering for unicast user plane data
options.B: To provide the key for deciphering broadcast assistance data
options.C: To authenticate the UE to the network
options.D: To synchronize ciphering algorithms between UE and MME

results.evidence: The Ciphering key data IE is used to transfer parameters that are needed for ciphering the SOR (Steering of Roaming) header and information, i.e., it provides the UE with the ciphering key, key index, and other parameters required to enable the USIM/ME to cipher or decipher SOR-related data (and, when applicable, UE parameters update data) sent via NAS signalling, as specified in clause 8.2.1.21 of 3GPP TS 24.301.

results.question: According to clause 8.2.1.21, the Ciphering key data IE is included for what type of data transmission?

options.A: Ciphered unicast control signalling
options.B: Ciphered broadcast assistance data
options.C: Emergency call establishment
options.D: Unciphered system information blocks

results.question: Which scenario triggers the UE behavior described in clause 6.5.1.7 for handling PDN connectivity requests when configured for dual priority?

options.A: When establishing the first PDN connection with any APN
options.B: When requesting a PDN connection with a different APN than any existing connection
options.C: When an existing PDN connection has low priority indicator 'MS is not configured for NAS signalling low priority' and a new request for the same APN has indicator 'MS is configured for NAS signalling low priority'
options.D: When the UE is in idle mode and requests any PDN connection

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.1.7, Handling PDN connectivity request for UE configured for dual priority
results.evidence: If the UE is configured for dual priority and has a PDN connectivity request pending (for which a low priority indication was included) for which no response has yet been received from the network, and the UE needs to initiate a new PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST for the same or a different APN with a normal priority (i.e. not subject to NAS signalling low priority), the UE shall be allowed to send the new PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message with the device properties IE indicating 'not configured for NAS signalling low priority', without waiting for the response to the previously sent low priority PDN connectivity request.

results.question: What alternative action can upper layers take instead of following the specific UE procedures for same-APN PDN connectivity requests with opposite low priority indicators?

options.A: Request establishment of a PDN connection with a different APN
options.B: Disable the dual priority configuration temporarily
options.C: Request deactivation of all existing PDN connections first
options.D: Use a different PDN type for the new connection request

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.1.7, Handling PDN connectivity request for UE configured for dual priority
results.evidence: As an alternative to following the specific UE procedures defined for handling a request from upper layers for a new PDN connection to an APN for which the UE already has a PDN connection established using the opposite value of the low priority indicator, the upper layers may decide not to request the establishment of the new PDN connection at all (i.e. the upper layers can simply refrain from requesting the additional PDN connectivity for the same APN with the conflicting low priority indicator setting), rather than requiring the UE to release/re-establish or otherwise reconcile the existing PDN connection.

options.A: EMM-DEREGISTERED
options.B: EMM-REGISTERED

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 4.4.1, what are the two primary security functions applied to EPS NAS messages between the UE and MME?

options.A: Authentication and Authorization
options.B: Integrity Protection and Ciphering
options.C: Firewalling and Deep Packet Inspection
options.D: Key Generation and Key Distribution

results.evidence: Once the EPS security context is established between the UE and MME, integrity protection of NAS messages is mandatory, and all NAS messages exchanged between the UE and the MME shall be integrity protected. Ciphering of NAS messages is optional but recommended, and if enabled, NAS messages shall also be ciphered. Thus, the two primary security functions applied to EPS NAS messages are: (1) integrity protection (using an integrity key and algorithm to compute a NAS-MAC/MAC value appended to the message, allowing verification that the message has not been altered and originates from a legitimate source), and (2) ciphering (encryption of the NAS message content using a ciphering key and algorithm to protect confidentiality of the signalling data), both derived from the EPS security context established via NAS security mode command procedure.

results.question: How does Clause 4.4.1 assume ciphering is handled for ease of description, and how is a network operated without it?

options.A: It assumes ciphering is never used; operation with ciphering requires configuring the MME to always select EEA1.
options.B: It assumes ciphering is optional per message; operation without ciphering requires the UE to request it.
options.C: It assumes ciphering is used unless stated otherwise; operation without ciphering uses the 'null ciphering algorithm' EEA0.
options.D: It assumes ciphering is mandated by the standard; operation without ciphering is not permitted.

results.evidence: For the purpose of the description in this clause it is assumed that the network does not indicate 'security protected message received' when establishing security protected NAS signalling connections, i.e. that the ciphering algorithm is included as one of the security algorithms in the security context. It is assumed in the present document that a network which enforces the use of ciphering does not send unciphered NAS messages to the UE and does not accept unciphered NAS messages from the UE. If the network operates without ciphering, this may be achieved by configuring the 'null ciphering algorithm' EEA0 (see subclause 4.4.5) as the selected ciphering algorithm in the security context, i.e. ciphering is formally applied to the NAS signalling but has no effect, as EEA0 involves no actual encryption/decryption of the message.

In this case, the mobile station classmark 2 IE indicates the mobile station classmark 2 information used for CS fallback and/or SMS over SGs, i.e. that the UE included in the ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message when the UE is registered for CS fallback and/or SMS over SGs and is capable of A/Gb mode or Iu mode.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.4.6, under what condition(s) must a UE include the MS network capability IE?

options.A: Only when supporting Iu mode
options.B: Only when supporting A/Gb mode
options.C: When supporting either A/Gb mode or Iu mode
options.D: When supporting neither A/Gb nor Iu mode

results.evidence: The MS network capability IE shall be included by the UE if the UE supports GERAN and/or UTRAN, i.e., the IE is included if the UE supports A/Gb mode or Iu mode.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the MS network capability IE as specified in TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.4.6?

options.A: To indicate the UE's location to the network
options.B: To indicate the UE's capabilities to the network
options.C: To request specific network services
options.D: To authenticate the UE to the network

results.evidence: The purpose of the MS network capability information element is to provide the network with information concerning aspects of the mobile station related to GPRS or Iu mode that are needed by the network when the mobile station has a GPRS or Iu mode capability, as specified in 3GPP TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.6, with reference to 3GPP TS 24.008.

results.question: What type of data can be transmitted to the UE using the Extended protocol configuration options IE according to clause 8.3.7.6?

options.A: Only authentication vectors and security parameters
options.B: Exclusively quality of service (QoS) parameters
options.C: Protocol data such as configuration parameters, error codes or messages/events
options.D: Only handover-related measurement reports

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.7.6, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: According to 3GPP TS 24.301 clause 8.3.7.6, the Extended protocol configuration options IE can be used by the network to transmit application‑specific data to the UE (i.e., data that is not related to session or bearer management, but is intended for use by an application running on the UE), in addition to the information otherwise conveyed for external PDN or network protocol configuration purposes (e.g., DNS server addresses, P-CSCF addresses, IPCP configuration for PPP-based PDN connections, and vendor-specific or operator-specific application data).

results.question: What does clause 8.3.7.6 specify as the purpose of including the Extended protocol configuration options IE?

options.A: To acknowledge receipt of UE capability information
options.B: To request the UE to provide additional protocol configuration options
options.C: For the network to transmit protocol data to the UE
options.D: To indicate successful PDN connection establishment

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.7.6, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The purpose of the Extended protocol configuration options information element is to transfer protocol configuration options that cannot be accommodated within the (non-extended) Protocol configuration options information element due to its length limitation, i.e. it is used whenever the protocol configuration options to be sent would exceed the maximum length supported by the Protocol configuration options IE, allowing the UE and the network to exchange additional configuration options, parameters or requests related to external packet data networks or other protocols associated with the PDN connection or EPS bearer context procedure in which it is included.

results.question: In which operational mode does TS 24.301 specify that the UE radio capability ID IE may be included when both the UE and network support RACS?

options.A: NB-S1 mode
options.B: WB-S1 mode
options.C: LTE-only mode
options.D: Dual-registration mode

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.26.25, UE radio capability ID
results.evidence: TS 24.301 specifies that when both the UE and the network support RACS (UE radio capability signalling optimisation), the UE radio capability ID IE may be included in the ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST messages while the UE is operating in S1 mode (i.e., attached to E-UTRAN/EPS), provided the UE holds a valid UE radio capability ID for the current PLMN and is not performing an emergency attach/registration.

results.question: Which of the following is NOT a required condition for including the UE radio capability ID IE in WB-S1 mode according to TS 24.301?

options.A: UE supports RACS
options.B: Network supports RACS
options.C: Network needs to assign a network-assigned UE radio capability ID
options.D: UE is in connected mode

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.26.25, UE radio capability ID
results.evidence: According to 3GPP TS 24.301, the UE radio capability ID IE is included in an ATTACH REQUEST / TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message while operating in WB-S1 mode only if ALL of the following are true: (a) the UE supports the UE radio capability ID related procedures; (b) the UE is operating in WB-S1 mode; (c) the network in the current tracking area has indicated (e.g., via broadcast system information) support for UE radio capability ID related procedures; and (d) the UE has a valid UE radio capability ID stored for the PLMN and access technology (RAT) combination of the current serving cell/registered PLMN. 'The UE is performing an attach/registration for emergency bearer services' is NOT one of these required conditions — emergency bearer service attach status has no bearing on whether the UE radio capability ID IE is included.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 5.6.1.3, upon receipt of which message(s) may the MME initiate EMM common procedures?

options.B: The SERVICE REQUEST, EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST, or CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST messages
options.C: Only the CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message
