results.evidence: Upon receipt of the SERVICE REQUEST message or the EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST message, the MME may initiate EMM common procedures, e.g. the EMM authentication and security mode control procedures.

results.question: As per TS 24.301 Clause 5.6.1.3, what is another example, besides authentication, of an EMM common procedure the MME may initiate?

options.A: Security mode control procedure
options.B: Handover procedure
options.C: Paging procedure
options.D: Location reporting procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.1.3, EMM common procedure initiation
results.evidence: The MME may also initiate other EMM common procedures during the service request procedure, e.g. security mode control procedure, identification procedure.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 6.6.3.1, what is the primary purpose of the Remote UE Report procedure?

options.A: To allow a remote UE to discover available ProSe UE-to-network relays
options.B: To enable a UE acting as ProSe UE-to-network relay to notify the network about remote UE connection status
options.C: To establish direct communication between two remote UEs without network involvement
options.D: To configure quality of service parameters for relayed connections

results.evidence: The purpose of the remote UE report procedure is to enable the ProSe UE-to-network relay UE to inform the network of the establishment or release of a PC5 connection with one or more remote UE(s), and to provide the network with information about those remote UE(s) (e.g. their identities and connection status), so that the network can maintain awareness of the remote UEs being served indirectly via the ProSe UE-to-network relay UE.

results.question: What specific events does the Remote UE Report procedure notify the network about, as defined in TS 24.301 Clause 6.6.3.1?

options.A: Remote UE authentication success or failure
options.B: Remote UE data usage thresholds being exceeded
options.C: Remote UE connection to or disconnection from the ProSe UE-to-network relay
options.D: Remote UE location changes during relay operation

results.evidence: The remote UE report procedure is used by the UE to notify the network that a remote UE has established or released a layer-2 link with the ProSe UE-to-network relay, i.e., to report a remote UE connected event or a remote UE disconnected event to the network.

results.question: Which type of UE initiates the Remote UE Report procedure according to TS 24.301 Clause 6.6.3.1?

options.A: Any UE within ProSe communication range
options.B: A remote UE seeking network connectivity
options.C: A UE acting as ProSe UE-to-network relay
options.D: The network's ProSe function entity

results.evidence: The remote UE report procedure is initiated by the UE acting as a ProSe UE-to-network relay to report information related to remote UE(s) connected via the relay to the network.

results.question: Where are the detailed specifications for remote UE connection and disconnection events referenced in TS 24.301 Clause 6.6.3.1?

options.A: 3GPP TS 24.334
options.B: 3GPP TS 23.303
options.C: 3GPP TS 36.300
options.D: 3GPP TS 33.303

results.evidence: The detailed specifications of the events related to connection and disconnection of remote UEs are specified in 3GPP TS 24.334.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.1.17, when is the 'Non-3GPP NW provided policies' information element included in a message?

options.A: Always, as it is a mandatory element for emergency call procedures
options.B: Only when the network needs to indicate whether emergency numbers provided via non-3GPP access can be used for UE detected emergency calls
options.C: When the UE is connected via both 3GPP and non-3GPP access simultaneously
options.D: When the network wants to override all UE emergency call policies

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.1.17, Non-3GPP NW provided policies
results.evidence: The Non-3GPP NW provided policies information element is included in the ATTACH ACCEPT message only if the UE indicated support for non-3GPP access network provided policies in the ATTACH REQUEST message and the network has such policies (e.g., ANDSF related information) available to provide to the UE.

results.question: What does the 'Non-3GPP NW provided policies' IE specifically indicate when included?

options.A: Whether the UE should prioritize 3GPP access for all emergency calls
options.B: Whether emergency numbers provided via non-3GPP access can be used to initiate UE detected emergency calls
options.C: A list of approved non-3GPP networks for emergency services
options.D: The maximum number of emergency calls allowed via non-3GPP access

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.1.17, Non-3GPP NW provided policies
results.evidence: The Non-3GPP NW provided policies IE, when included, indicates that the UE is allowed to perform WLAN selection using the ANDSF/non-3GPP access network discovery and selection related information provided by a non-3GPP access network (e.g., WLAN) rather than requiring information solely from the 3GPP system, in accordance with the policies specified in TS 24.312.

results.question: How should a UE interpret the absence of the 'Non-3GPP NW provided policies' IE?

options.A: As an error condition requiring re-establishment of the connection
options.B: As an indication that non-3GPP emergency numbers cannot be used under any circumstances
options.C: As receipt of an IE with all bits of the value part coded as zero
options.D: As permission to use any available emergency numbers regardless of source

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.1.17, Non-3GPP NW provided policies
results.evidence: If the Non-3GPP NW provided policies IE is not included in the ATTACH ACCEPT message or in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, the UE shall interpret this as if the network does not support provisioning of non-3GPP access network selection and inter-system mobility policies via NAS signalling, i.e. the UE shall behave as if no such policies are configured by the network and shall use any locally stored or pre-configured ANDSF/inter-system mobility policies instead.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the 'Non-3GPP NW provided policies' information element as specified in TS 24.301?

options.A: To provide routing information for emergency calls via non-3GPP networks
options.B: To indicate whether UE detected emergency calls can use emergency numbers provided via non-3GPP access
options.C: To authenticate non-3GPP networks for emergency service provision
options.D: To configure UE policies for all non-3GPP network interactions

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.1.17, Non-3GPP NW provided policies
results.evidence: The Non-3GPP NW provided policies information element indicates whether the UE is permitted to use non-3GPP access network (e.g., WLAN) provided policy information—rather than or in addition to ANDSF policies—for traffic steering and access network selection decisions (e.g., WLAN selection/offload). It is a single-bit value IE included by the network in EMM messages (such as ATTACH ACCEPT/TAU ACCEPT) to convey this authorization to the UE.

results.question: Under what condition must a UE stop timer T3396 associated with no APN when handling ESM cause #26 with a Back-off timer value?

options.A: When the timer value indicates neither zero nor deactivated, an APN was included, and the request type was 'emergency'.
options.B: When the timer value indicates neither zero nor deactivated, no APN was included, and the request type was different from 'emergency' and 'handover of emergency bearer services'.
options.C: When the timer value is zero, no APN was included, and the request type was 'handover of emergency bearer services'.
options.D: When the timer value is deactivated, an APN was included, and the request type was 'emergency'.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.1.4.2, Handling of network rejection due to ESM cause #26
results.evidence: If the UE receives a PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT, PDN DISCONNECT REQUEST, ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST, or other ESM message containing ESM cause #26 'insufficient resources' together with a Back-off timer value IE, and that message does not contain an APN, the UE shall stop timer T3396 if it is already running and (re)start it with the received value, associating this instance of the timer with 'no APN' and storing it together with the PLMN identity. The UE shall stop this timer T3396 associated with no APN, if running, when the UE is switched off, when the USIM is removed, or when the UE enters the EMM-DEREGISTERED state (i.e., de-registers from the EPS network in that PLMN), since the back-off restriction associated with 'no APN' is no longer applicable once the UE loses its EMM registration context.

results.question: When a UE switches off and then back on while timer T3396 was running, and the elapsed time 't' is greater than the remaining time 't1', what must the UE do with timer T3396?

options.A: The timer need not be restarted.
options.B: The timer shall be restarted with the original full timer value.
options.C: The timer shall be restarted with the value t1 minus t.
options.D: The timer shall be restarted with the value t1.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.1.4.2, Handling of network rejection due to ESM cause #26
results.evidence: If timer T3396 is running when the UE is switched off, and the UE is switched on again before the timer expires, the UE shall start T3396 with the same value initially set if 't' is greater than 't1', where 't' is the time elapsed since the UE was switched off and 't1' is the value of the remaining time when the UE was switched off.

results.question: If a UE is not capable of determining the elapsed time 't' between switch off and switch on while timer T3396 was running, how must it restart the timer?

options.A: The UE shall not restart the timer.
options.B: The UE shall restart the timer with a random value within the original range.
options.C: The UE shall restart the timer with the original full timer value.
options.D: The UE shall restart the timer with the value t1.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.1.4.2, Handling of network rejection due to ESM cause #26
results.evidence: If the UE is not able to determine the elapsed time while switch off, the UE shall behave as if timer T3396 has expired at the time of switching off, i.e. the UE shall restart the timer T3396 with its initial value upon switching on.

results.question: Under what condition is a network required to include the Radio Priority IE when supporting mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode?

options.A: If the UE supports Iu mode
options.B: If the UE supports A/Gb mode
options.C: If the UE supports S1 mode only
options.D: If the network supports A/Gb mode only

results.evidence: If the network supports mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode, the network shall include the radio priority IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT message and the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message if radio priority for CS fallback establishment is included in the ATTACH ACCEPT message or the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, or if the UE has indicated support for dual priority in the ATTACH REQUEST message or the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 6.4.4.4, what action must a UE take when requested to deactivate the default EPS bearer of its last PDN connection, if EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection is NOT supported by the UE or MME?

options.A: Proceed with the normal deactivation procedure as specified in clause 6.4.4.3.
options.B: Ignore the request and maintain the bearer context.
options.C: Respond by performing a detach procedure and should perform an attach procedure.
options.D: Initiate a new PDN connection request to establish an alternate default bearer before deactivation.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.4.4, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.evidence: If the EPS bearer identity is mapped to the default EPS bearer context of the last PDN connection and EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection is not supported by the UE or the MME, the UE, in state EMM-REGISTERED, shall locally deactivate the PDN connection after the deactivation of the EPS bearer context without peer-to-peer NAS signalling, and shall enter state EMM-DEREGISTERED after the deactivation of the EPS bearer context.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 6.5.3.6, what action should the MME take when it receives a BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REQUEST message containing a linked EPS bearer identity that does not belong to the default EPS bearer context of an established PDN connection?

options.A: Initiate a new PDN connection procedure
options.B: Reply with BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REJECT with ESM cause #43 'invalid EPS bearer identity'
options.C: Ignore the message and wait for retransmission
options.D: Reply with BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REJECT with ESM cause #31 'request rejected, unspecified'

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.3.6, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: Upon receipt of a BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REQUEST message, if the linked EPS bearer identity does not belong to the default EPS bearer context of an established PDN connection, the MME shall send a BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REJECT message with the ESM cause value #43 'invalid EPS bearer identity'.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 5.1.3.3, where is the EPS update status stored when the corresponding file is NOT present in the USIM?

options.A: In the volatile memory of the ME
options.B: In the non-volatile memory of the ME
options.C: In the HSS database
options.D: In the MME's temporary cache

results.evidence: If the USIM is not updated with EPS update status the corresponding EPS update status information stored in the ME shall be deleted, if any. If the EPS update status is not stored in the USIM, the EPS update status shall be stored in a non-volatile memory in the ME together with the GUTI, the last visited registered TAI, if available, and the TAI list, so that this information is retained when the MS is switched off and is retained also, when the battery is detached from the MS, or the UICC is removed.

results.question: Which EPS update status would be set when the MME provides a negative answer due to subscription restrictions?

options.A: EU1
options.B: EU2
options.C: EU3
options.D: EU4

results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.5.3.2.5: If the TRACKING AREA UPDATING REJECT message is received with EMM cause #7 'EPS services not allowed' (indicating a negative answer due to subscription restrictions from the network/HSS), the UE shall set the EPS update status to EU2 NOT UPDATED, delete the list of equivalent PLMNs, and enter state EMM-DEREGISTERED.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.20.4, when must the Protocol configuration options IE be included in a message from the UE?

options.A: When the UE is in NB-S1 mode and wishes to transmit protocol data
options.B: When the UE wishes to transmit protocol data, is in WB-S1 mode, the requested PDN Type is non-IP, and the APN is not for UAS services
options.C: When the UE wishes to transmit protocol data, is in WB-S1 mode, the requested PDN Type is different from non-IP and Ethernet, and the requested APN is not for UAS services
options.D: When the Extended protocol configuration options IE is also included in the same message

results.question: Under which specific UE capability condition must the Protocol configuration options IE be included, according to the second set of criteria in Clause 8.3.20.4?

options.A: When the UE supports emergency services fallback
options.B: When the UE supports local IP address in traffic flow aggregate description and TFT filter
options.C: When the UE supports multiple PDN connections
options.D: When the UE supports Ethernet PDN type

results.evidence: The network shall include the Protocol configuration options IE, if the UE included this IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, and additionally, if the UE supports the northbound interface for accessing PCO content, i.e. the UE indicated support for the northbound interface in the UE network capability IE during the attach or tracking area updating procedure, the network shall include the Protocol configuration options IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT message.

results.question: When is the Protocol configuration options IE explicitly prohibited from being included in a message?

options.A: When the UE is in WB-S1 mode
options.B: When the requested APN is for UAS services
options.C: When the Extended protocol configuration options IE is included in the message
options.D: When the requested PDN Type is Ethernet

results.evidence: The network shall not include the Protocol configuration options IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT, ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST, or other relevant NAS messages if the UE has indicated it does not support the transfer of protocol configuration options; more specifically, per TS 24.301, the UE shall not include the Protocol configuration options IE in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message if the PDN type is set to 'non-IP' and no protocol configuration options are needed, and the network shall not include this IE when it has no protocol configuration options to transfer, i.e., its inclusion is conditional and it is explicitly prohibited when there is nothing to convey or when the underlying PDN connection type does not support such configuration transfer (e.g., for Emergency PDN connections in certain conditions).

results.question: When enhanced coverage use is restricted for a UE, where must it refrain from using enhanced coverage?

options.A: Only in the registered PLMN
options.B: Only in PLMNs not in the equivalent PLMN list
options.C: In the registered PLMN and any PLMN in the equivalent PLMN list
options.D: Only when in NB-S1 mode, regardless of PLMN

results.evidence: If enhanced coverage restriction applies to the UE, the UE shall not use enhanced coverage for transmission on the NAS signalling connection or for transmission of user data, when accessing the network via E-UTRAN in either WB-S1 mode or NB-S1 mode.

results.question: According to clause 5.3.16, under what condition does the network calculate applicable NAS timer values as described in clause 4.8 for a UE supporting CE mode B?

options.A: When enhanced coverage use is restricted for the UE
options.B: When CE mode B is restricted for the UE
options.C: When the UE does not indicate support for restriction on use of enhanced coverage
options.D: When enhanced coverage use is not restricted OR CE mode B is not restricted for the UE

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.16, Restriction on use of enhanced coverage
results.evidence: If the UE indicates support for CE mode B, then the network calculates the applicable NAS timer values as described in clause 4.8 based on the UE's use of CE mode B.

results.question: Under what condition may a UE initiate an attach procedure for emergency bearer services when timer T3346 is active?

options.A: When the UE is configured to use AC11-15 in the selected PLMN
options.B: When entering a new PLMN that is not equivalent to the PLMN where T3346 started
options.C: For emergency bearer services, even if timer T3346 is running
options.D: When the tracking area changes and T3346 is not running

results.evidence: The UE may initiate the attach procedure for emergency bearer services even if timer T3346 is running, i.e., the UE is allowed to start the attach procedure for emergency bearer services regardless of the state of timer T3346 (3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.5.1.2.3).

results.question: When must a UE initiate an attach or combined attach procedure upon entering a new PLMN while timer T3346 is running?

options.A: Always, regardless of PLMN equivalence or forbidden lists
options.B: Only if the new PLMN is equivalent to the PLMN where T3346 started
options.C: If the new PLMN is not equivalent, and its PLMN identity and tracking area are not in forbidden lists
options.D: Only if timer T3346 is not running

results.question: What triggers a UE to initiate an attach procedure for transmitting user data related to an exceptional event?

options.A: A request from upper layers to establish a PDN connection for RLOS
options.B: A request from upper layers to transmit exceptional event data, if allowed and T3346 is not already running for 'MO exception data'
options.C: The expiry of timer T3411, T3402, or T3346
options.D: A request for non-EPS services for emergency call from CM layers

results.evidence: The UE shall initiate the attach procedure if the UE, in state EMM-DEREGISTERED, needs to transmit user data related to an exceptional event and is not attached for EPS services (3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.5.1.2.2).

results.question: When the EPS bearer context modification procedure is initiated by the network, what mandatory information element must the MME include in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message to identify the specific context?

options.A: Procedure transaction identity (PTI)
options.B: EPS bearer identity
options.C: Header compression configuration IE
options.D: UE network capability IE

results.evidence: The MME initiates the EPS bearer context modification procedure by sending a MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message to the UE, including the EPS bearer identity IE, which identifies the EPS bearer context to be modified, and starts timer T3486.

results.question: Under what condition must the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message contain the procedure transaction identity (PTI) value?

options.A: When the UE supports Control plane CIoT EPS optimization
options.B: When the procedure was initiated by a UE requested bearer resource allocation or modification procedure
options.C: When timer T3486 is started
options.D: When the MME enters BEARER CONTEXT MODIFY PENDING state

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.3.2, EPS bearer context modification initiated by the network
results.evidence: The network shall include the PTI in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message if the EPS bearer context modification procedure was initiated as part of the UE or network requested bearer resource modification procedure.

results.question: When may the MME include the Header compression configuration IE in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message during EPS bearer context modification?

options.A: Always, as it is mandatory for bearer modification
options.B: Only when the UE is in idle mode
options.C: When specific CIoT EPS optimization capabilities are indicated by the UE and supported by the MME
options.D: When the procedure was initiated by the network without UE request

results.question: Under what specific condition is the UE required to include the 'Old location area identification' IE during a combined tracking area updating procedure?

options.A: If it is performing an emergency registration
options.B: If it has a valid location area identification
options.C: If the network supports 5G core

results.evidence: The UE shall include the Old location area identification IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message only if the UE is performing a combined tracking area updating procedure (i.e., the EPS update type IE indicates 'combined TA/LA updating' or 'combined TA/LA updating with IMSI attach') and the UE holds a valid LAI (i.e., the UE has a valid location area identification stored from a previous successful location/routing/tracking area update or attach in that location area).

results.question: What must be true about the UE's location area identification for it to include the 'Old location area identification' IE in the specified procedure?

options.A: It must be invalid or expired
options.B: It must be newly assigned
options.C: It must be valid
options.D: It must be from a different PLMN
