results.evidence: The MS shall include the Old location area identification IE in the LOCATION UPDATING REQUEST message if the MS has a valid LAI (i.e., if the LAI stored in the MS is different from the deleted or invalid value); this IE indicates the location area identification of the location area in which the MS was previously registered or last updated, and is used by the network to determine whether the update is a location area update or a periodic update, and to support IMSI attach or normal location updating procedures.

results.question: According to clause 8.2.29.13, when does the UE include the 'Old location area identification' IE?

options.A: In all tracking area updating procedures
options.B: Only in emergency procedures
options.C: During a combined tracking area updating procedure with a valid LAI
options.D: When transitioning from idle to connected mode

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.13, Old location area identification
results.evidence: The UE shall include the Old location area identification IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message if the UE holds a valid location area identification (LAI), i.e. when the tracking area updating procedure is performed due to an inter-system change from A/Gb mode or Iu mode to S1 mode and the UE has a valid LAI stored from its previous GERAN/UTRAN registration.

results.question: How is the UE's location known to the MME when the UE is in EMM-IDLE mode while in the EMM-REGISTERED state?

options.A: With the accuracy of a serving eNodeB.
options.B: With the accuracy of a single, precise tracking area.
options.C: With the accuracy of a list of tracking areas.
options.D: The location is not known; the MME must page the UE to discover it.

results.evidence: In EMM-REGISTERED state, when the UE is in EMM-IDLE mode, the network has, in general, no knowledge of the actual location of the UE, but only knows the tracking area(s) in which the UE has registered or in which the UE is expected to be located (i.e. the tracking area(s) contained in the last TAI list assigned to the UE).

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 4.6.1, what procedures must a relay node support?

options.A: Only procedures specific to relay node functionality
options.B: All procedures mandatory for a UE supporting S1 mode only
options.C: A subset of UE procedures selected by network configuration
options.D: Only procedures defined in relay-specific sections of the specification

results.evidence: A relay node shall support the following procedures specified in this specification: - the attach procedure; - the tracking area updating procedure; - the GUTI reallocation procedure; - the authentication procedure; - the security mode control procedure; - the service request procedure; and - the detach procedure. When acting as a UE towards the network, the relay node shall behave as specified for a UE in this specification, unless stated otherwise.

results.question: When the specification mentions requirements for a 'relay node' rather than a 'UE' in TS 24.301 Clause 4.6.1, what does this indicate?

options.A: The requirement applies to all UEs in relay-assisted communication
options.B: The functionality is only applicable to relay nodes
options.C: The requirement is optional for both UEs and relay nodes
options.D: The specification contains an error and should use 'UE' consistently

results.evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.6.1 (General): "Unless otherwise stated, all the EMM and ESM procedures specified for the UE apply also to a relay node (RN). Where a requirement is stated for a relay node instead of the UE, this requirement applies only when the UE is acting as a relay node as defined in 3GPP TS 36.300 [3], and not to a UE operating in normal (non-relay) mode."

results.question: Based on TS 24.301 Clause 4.6.1, which statement correctly describes a relay node's procedural requirements?

options.A: A relay node implements a completely different set of procedures than a UE
options.B: A relay node supports mandatory UE S1 mode procedures plus additional relay-specific functionality
options.C: A relay node only implements procedures where the term 'relay node' is explicitly used
options.D: A relay node's procedures are determined solely by the serving gateway

results.evidence: TS 24.301 Clause 4.6.1 specifies that if the UE is a relay node (RN), it shall indicate this to the network by setting the Device properties information element to 'UE is a relay node' in the ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST messages. The network, upon receiving this indication, shall apply relay-node-specific handling, such as not invoking non-RN-applicable procedures (e.g. certain SMS, CS fallback, or voice domain preference handling) and using RN-specific configuration where required.

results.question: Upon receiving a BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST message, what does the MME verify first to determine if the UE's requested resources can be established, modified, or released?

options.A: The UE's current location and tracking area
options.B: The EPS bearer identity given in the EPS bearer identity for packet filter IE
options.C: The QoS parameters in the requested bearer resource
options.D: The PTI value matching an ongoing procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.4.3, UE requested bearer resource modification procedure accepted by the network
results.evidence: Upon receipt of the BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST message, if the message contains an EPS bearer identity for TFT and the linked EPS bearer identity IE, the MME shall check whether it has a PDN connection to which the requested traffic flow aggregate can be associated. The MME determines this by checking the linked EPS bearer identity and, if the EPS bearer context indicated by the EPS bearer identity for TFT is a dedicated EPS bearer context, the MME shall also verify that the EPS bearer identity for TFT is associated with an EPS bearer that belongs to the same PDN connection as the linked EPS bearer identity. The MME shall verify whether the requested traffic flow aggregate can be accepted by the network, and whether the requested QoS and, if included, the requested APN aggregate maximum bit rate can be provided by checking whether the requested resources are compatible with the current EPS bearer context(s) and can be supported by the network.

results.question: When a bearer resource modification request asks to release resources such that the TFT contains only uplink packet filters, what may the network do?

options.A: Must initiate an EPS bearer context deactivation procedure
options.B: May initiate an EPS bearer context deactivation procedure
options.C: Must initiate an EPS bearer context modification procedure
options.D: Shall reject the request and send a failure cause

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.4.3, UE requested bearer resource modification procedure accepted by the network
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.4 (UE requested bearer resource modification procedure): 'If the UE requests the release of packet filters and this results in the traffic flow template of the affected EPS bearer context containing only uplink packet filters, the network may deactivate the EPS bearer context using the EPS bearer context deactivation procedure instead of modifying it.'

results.question: After successful dedicated EPS bearer context activation following a BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST, when the network modifies the context to delete certain packet filters, what PTI value must the MME set in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST?

options.A: The same PTI as the original BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST
options.B: A new, unique PTI value
options.C: "no procedure transaction identity assigned"
options.D: PTI value 0

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.4.3, UE requested bearer resource modification procedure accepted by the network
results.evidence: If the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message is used to delete packet filters from the traffic flow aggregate but not to delete the traffic flow aggregate of a dedicated EPS bearer context, and it is sent to indicate the successful completion of the network-requested bearer resource modification procedure due to a UE requested bearer resource modification procedure being triggered by a BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST message, the network shall set the PTI in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message to the value indicated by the UE in the PTI IE of the BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST message.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the NBIFOM container information element in 3GPP TS 24.301?

options.A: To transfer information associated with network-based IP flow mobility
options.B: To establish the default EPS bearer context
options.C: To manage UE radio capability updates
options.D: To carry authentication vectors for network access

results.evidence: The NBIFOM container information element (IE) is used to transparently carry NBIFOM (Network-Based IP Flow Mobility) protocol content between the UE and the network within ESM NAS messages (e.g., PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST, ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE, ACTIVATE DEFAULT/DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST/ACCEPT, MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST/ACCEPT, and DEACTIVATE EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST). Its primary purpose is to enable the exchange of NBIFOM-specific information—such as NBIFOM mode, NBIFOM supported indication, routing rules, and routing filters—so that the UE and the network can negotiate and manage the routing of IP flows belonging to a single PDN connection across multiple accesses (e.g., 3GPP access and WLAN) in a network-controlled or UE/NW-initiated manner, without the core network needing to interpret the detailed NBIFOM content itself, which is instead processed by the underlying NBIFOM functionality as defined in 3GPP TS 24.161.

results.question: Which 3GPP specification is referenced in Clause 8.3.9.5 for details on network-based IP flow mobility?

options.A: 3GPP TS 24.161
options.B: 3GPP TS 23.401
options.C: 3GPP TS 36.331
options.D: 3GPP TS 33.401

results.evidence: 3GPP TS 23.261 specifies the details on network-based IP flow mobility, and clause 8.3.9.5 references this specification for the relevant procedures.

results.question: In the abnormal case on the fifth expiry of timer T3482 for a non-emergency PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST, what is the specified UE behavior?

options.A: Resend the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST and reset/restart T3482 for one final attempt.
options.B: Inform upper layers of the failure and initiate local detach procedures.
options.C: Abort the procedure, release the allocated PTI, and enter the state PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE.
options.D: Switch to emergency bearer services procedures and restart the request.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.1.5, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.evidence: e) On the fifth expiry of timer T3482 for a non-emergency PDN connectivity request, the UE shall abort the procedure, release the PDN connectivity procedure transaction identity allocated for the request, and shall inform the ESM sublayer that the PDN connectivity request procedure failed. If the PDN connectivity request procedure was triggered due to receiving a request from upper layers, the UE shall inform the upper layers about the failure of the procedure.

results.question: During which procedures may a UE supporting UAS services request a PDN connection for USS communication?

options.A: Only during attach procedure
options.B: Only during UE-requested PDN connectivity procedure
options.C: During both attach and UE-requested PDN connectivity procedures
options.D: Only during network-initiated bearer modification

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.13.2, Authentication and authorization of UAV
results.evidence: The UE may request the establishment of a PDN connection for USS communication during the PDN connectivity procedure (i.e. UE requested PDN connectivity procedure) or during the attach procedure, by including the 'PDN connection for USS communication' indication in the PCO or in the request type/ESM information, as specified for UAS services in TS 24.301.

results.question: How does a UE provide the CAA-level UAV ID to the network when requesting a PDN connection for USS communication?

options.A: Via the APN field in the PDN connectivity request
options.B: Via the protocol configuration options
options.C: Via the EPS bearer identity
options.D: Via the UE network capability information element

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.13.2, Authentication and authorization of UAV
results.evidence: When the UE requests a PDN connection to be used for USS communication, if the UE holds a CAA-level UAV ID, the UE shall include the CAA-level UAV ID in the ESM message container information element or the Protocol configuration options information element of the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message, as specified for the corresponding Aerial UE subscription information procedures, in order to provide the CAA-level UAV ID to the network for USS communication (e.g., for the purpose of UAS (Unmanned Aerial System) services authorization and identification).

results.question: What action may the network take after a successful UUAA-SM procedure for a UE supporting UAS services?

options.A: Immediately release the PDN connection for USS communication
options.B: Initiate re-authentication or re-authorization as part of network-initiated EPS bearer context modification
options.C: Force the UE to perform a new attach procedure
options.D: Disable all non-UAS services on the UE

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.13.2, Authentication and authorization of UAV
results.evidence: After a successful UUAA-SM procedure, the network may initiate the establishment of a PDN connection (e.g., using the network requested PDN connectivity procedure) to enable the UE to communicate with the UAS Service Supplier (USS) for C2 communication, and may include the USS address and/or CAA-level UAV ID in the relevant ESM signalling (e.g., the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST or PDN CONNECTIVITY ACCEPT message).

results.question: Under what condition is the Extended EPS QoS IE included in a message according to TS 24.301 clause 8.3.3.11?

options.A: When the network wants to transmit any QoS parameters to the UE
options.B: When the network wishes to transmit maximum and guaranteed bit rate values and at least one exceeds the maximum specified in the EPS QoS IE
options.C: When the UE requests enhanced QoS capabilities during attachment
options.D: When the network supports 5G QoS parameters in EPS sessions

results.evidence: The extended EPS quality of service IE is included in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message if the default EPS bearer context is associated with parameter values that are not supported by the EPS QoS IE (i.e. the bit rates or the maximum bit rates exceed the maximum value encoded in the EPS QoS IE).

results.question: What triggers the inclusion of the Extended EPS QoS IE based on the bit rate values?

options.A: When both maximum and guaranteed bit rates are below the EPS QoS IE maximum
options.B: When at least one bit rate value exceeds the maximum specified in the EPS QoS IE
options.C: When the UE reports insufficient bit rates in measurements
options.D: When the network implements QoS pre-emption procedures

results.evidence: The Extended EPS QoS IE shall be included by the network (and, for EPS bearer context modification, may be included) whenever the value of any of the bit rate parameters of the EPS QoS – i.e. the Maximum Bit Rate for uplink, Maximum Bit Rate for downlink, Guaranteed Bit Rate for uplink, or Guaranteed Bit Rate for downlink – exceeds the range that can be encoded in the EPS QoS IE (3GPP TS 24.008 subclause 10.5.6.5), i.e. when any of these bit rates is greater than 1000 kbps (as encoded in octets 7 to 9 of the EPS QoS IE) up to the maximum value of 256 Mbps, or when any bit rate value requires the extended range up to 10 Gbps as defined for the 'extended maximum bit rate' and 'extended guaranteed bit rate' fields. In such cases, the EPS QoS IE shall encode the bit rate using the value '0xFF' (indicating that the extended value is used), and the actual bit rate value shall be conveyed in the corresponding octets of the Extended EPS QoS IE.

results.question: Which of the following accurately describes the network's intent when including the Extended EPS QoS IE?

options.A: To indicate QoS parameters for emergency bearer services
options.B: To transmit maximum and guaranteed bit rate values to the UE
options.C: To downgrade the QoS for power saving purposes
options.D: To synchronize QoS parameters with the 5G core network

results.evidence: The network includes the Extended EPS QoS IE to indicate additional or extended EPS QoS parameters (e.g., extended maximum bit rates for uplink and downlink, extended guaranteed bit rates for uplink and downlink) that cannot be represented by the EPS QoS IE alone, thereby allowing the network to signal bit rate values beyond the range supported by the standard EPS QoS IE when activating or modifying an EPS bearer context.

results.question: What is the relationship between the Extended EPS QoS IE and the EPS QoS IE maximum values?

options.A: The Extended EPS QoS IE is always included alongside the EPS QoS IE
options.B: The Extended EPS QoS IE is included when bit rate values fall within EPS QoS IE limits
options.C: The Extended EPS QoS IE is included when bit rate values exceed EPS QoS IE maximums
options.D: The Extended EPS QoS IE replaces the EPS QoS IE for all QoS signaling

results.evidence: The Extended EPS QoS IE is used to specify the maximum bit rates and guaranteed bit rates for uplink and downlink when the value of these parameters exceeds the value range supported by the EPS QoS IE (i.e., when the bit rate is greater than 1000 Mbps, which is the maximum value that can be represented in the EPS QoS IE). Thus, the Extended EPS QoS IE extends the range of values that can be signalled beyond the maximum values (1000 Mbps) supported by the EPS QoS IE described in subclause 9.9.4.3.

results.question: Under what condition is the Mobile station classmark 3 information element (IE) included in a message according to TS 24.301?

options.A: If the UE supports emergency call fallback
options.B: If the UE supports SRVCC to GERAN
options.C: If the UE is operating in single radio mode
options.D: If the UE supports VoLTE

results.evidence: The Mobile station classmark 3 IE is included by the UE if the UE supports GERAN and the value part of the Mobile station classmark 2 IE together with the network's request/support conditions require it; specifically, it shall be included if the UE supports GERAN and either the network indicates support for it or the UE needs to convey additional radio capability information for GERAN, as specified in TS 24.301, e.g., in TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST and other relevant messages when GERAN capabilities need to be signalled to the network.

results.question: What specific SRVCC capability necessitates the inclusion of the Mobile station classmark 3 IE per clause 8.2.4.10?

options.A: SRVCC from E-UTRAN to UTRAN
options.B: SRVCC from UTRAN to GERAN
options.C: SRVCC to GERAN
options.D: SRVCC from GERAN to E-UTRAN

results.evidence: The MS shall include the Mobile station classmark 3 IE in the ATTACH REQUEST message, if it supports UE-to-network relay operation... more specifically, the Mobile station classmark 3 IE is included if the UE supports CS fallback and SRVCC, i.e. if the UE indicates support for 'SRVCC from E-UTRAN to UTRAN/GERAN'. This capability requires the network to know the UE's UTRAN/GERAN classmark information, which is conveyed via the Mobile station classmark 3 IE, in order to perform the SRVCC handover procedure to a 3G/2G CS domain.

results.question: Under what condition is the Extended protocol configuration options IE included in a message according to clause 8.3.22.3?

options.A: When the network wishes to transmit protocol data to the UE
options.B: When the UE wishes to transmit protocol data to the network and extended PCO is supported end-to-end
options.C: When any protocol configuration needs to be updated, regardless of support
options.D: When the PDN connection is being established for the first time

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.22.3, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The extended protocol configuration options IE is included if the network or the UE, respectively, needs to transfer information that cannot be transferred in the (extended) protocol configuration options IE due to the limitation of the length of the (extended) protocol configuration options IE.

results.question: What type of data can the UE transmit using the Extended protocol configuration options IE as described in clause 8.3.22.3?

options.A: Only authentication parameters
options.B: Only error codes
options.C: Protocol data such as configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events
options.D: Only session management commands

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.22.3, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The Extended protocol configuration options IE may be used to transmit additional data related to a specific protocol, such as data related to PDN connection establishment, e.g. DNS server addresses, P-CSCF addresses, or data used for transferring information between the UE and the PDN, e.g. for supporting DHCPv4/DHCPv6 based address allocation, or for carrying container(s) for exchanging information related to specific protocols such as PCO for PCSCF discovery, and can also be used to transfer higher layer signalling messages between the UE and the network, such as protocol configuration options related to non-IP data transfer or for exchanging application-level configuration information.

results.question: How does the structure of the SERVICE REQUEST message compare to a standard layer 3 message?

options.A: It follows the standard layer 3 message structure exactly
options.B: Its structure does not follow the structure of a standard layer 3 message
options.C: It uses a proprietary structure defined by the UE manufacturer
options.D: It is identical to the ATTACH REQUEST message structure

results.evidence: The SERVICE REQUEST message does not follow the structure of a standard layer 3 message as defined in subclause 9.1.2. Specifically, it does not contain the sequence number, or the security header type and protocol discriminator in the same way; instead, it is designed as a short message to minimize signalling overhead, containing only the message type IEI-less identity, KSI, sequence number, and short MAC, without the full standard header fields such as EPS bearer identity or transaction identifier that appear in other messages.

results.question: Under what primary condition does the network initiate paging for EPS services using IMSI with CN domain indicator set to 'PS'?

options.A: When the UE is in idle mode to conserve battery
options.B: When the S-TMSI is not available due to a network failure
options.C: When performing regular location updates
options.D: When the UE requests a service type change

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.2.2.2, Paging for EPS services through E-UTRAN using IMSI
results.evidence: The network shall initiate paging for EPS services using IMSI, with the CN domain indicator set to 'PS', if the network does not hold a valid GUTI (or S-TMSI) for the UE, i.e., when the UE's EMM context has been deleted or is otherwise unavailable at the network side, such as after the MME has lost the mapping between the UE's identity and its temporary identifiers.

results.question: What is the first action a UE must take upon receiving a paging for EPS services using IMSI, according to the specified procedure?

options.A: Delete the GUTI and KSIASME parameters
options.B: Stop timer T3346 if it is running
options.C: Set the EPS update status to EU2 NOT UPDATED
options.D: Locally deactivate any EPS bearer context(s)

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.2.2.2, Paging for EPS services through E-UTRAN using IMSI
results.evidence: Upon receiving a paging for EPS services using IMSI, the UE shall stop timer T3446, if running, and locally deactivate the ISR (if ISR was activated), then proceed with an EPS attach procedure.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 5.5.1.3.4.1, what does the EPS attach result IE value indicating 'combined EPS/IMSI attach' signify about the attach procedure?

options.A: Attach for EPS services was successful, but attach for non-EPS services failed
options.B: Attach for EPS services failed, but attach for non-EPS services was successful
options.C: Attach for both EPS and non-EPS services, or for EPS services and 'SMS only', was successful
options.D: Attach for non-EPS services was successful, but attach for EPS services and 'SMS only' failed

results.evidence: If the EPS attach result IE value indicates 'combined EPS/IMSI attach', this means that the network has accepted the UE's request for a combined EPS/IMSI attach and that both EPS services and non-EPS (i.e. IMSI, CS domain) services have been successfully activated. The UE shall then consider itself to be attached to both EPS and non-EPS services, i.e. it shall proceed as if the attach type indicated in the ATTACH REQUEST message had been 'combined EPS/IMSI attach' and act accordingly for further mobility management and session management procedures (e.g., setting the TIN to 'GUTI', enabling CS fallback and SMS over SGs, and expecting a location area identity in the ATTACH ACCEPT message).

results.question: When the EPS attach result IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT message indicates 'EPS only', what is the status of the attach for non-EPS services or 'SMS only'?

options.A: It was successful
options.B: It failed
options.C: It is still pending
options.D: It was not attempted

results.evidence: The EPS attach result IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT message indicates whether the network has accepted the UE's attach request for EPS services only, or for EPS services and non-EPS services (combined EPS/IMSI attach), or for 'SMS only'. If the EPS attach result IE value indicates 'EPS only', this means that the network has accepted the attach request only for EPS services, and the attach for non-EPS services (i.e., combined EPS/IMSI attach) has not been accepted; consequently, the UE is not attached for non-EPS services and the 'SMS only' status does not apply, as the UE is registered for EPS services only.

results.question: Based on TS 24.301 Clause 5.5.1.3.4.1, which EPS attach result IE value indicates that attach for EPS services has been successful?

options.A: Only 'combined EPS/IMSI attach' indicates this
options.B: Only 'EPS only' indicates this
options.C: Both 'combined EPS/IMSI attach' and 'EPS only' indicate this
options.D: Neither 'combined EPS/IMSI attach' nor 'EPS only' indicate this

results.evidence: In the ATTACH ACCEPT message, the EPS attach result IE value 'EPS only' indicates that the attach for EPS services only has been accepted by the network, and the value 'combined EPS/IMSI attach' indicates that the attach for EPS services has been successful and, additionally, combined EPS/IMSI attach has been accepted.

results.question: If the EPS attach result IE indicates 'combined EPS/IMSI attach', which of the following scenarios is possible according to TS 24.301 Clause 5.5.1.3.4.1?

options.A: Attach for EPS services failed, but attach for non-EPS services was successful
options.B: Attach for EPS services and 'SMS only' was successful
options.C: Attach for EPS services was successful, but attach for non-EPS services failed
options.D: Attach for non-EPS services was successful, but attach for 'SMS only' failed

results.evidence: TS 24.301 clause 5.5.1.3.4.1 states that if the EPS attach result IE value indicates 'combined EPS/IMSI attach', it is possible that the network has accepted the attach request for EPS services only, even though the UE requested combined EPS/IMSI attach. In this case, the MME includes the EMM cause value #16 'combined attach not successful, but EPS attach is possible' (or an equivalent CS-domain related cause) in the ATTACH ACCEPT message. The UE shall then treat the attach as successful for EPS services only, and shall not consider itself attached for non-EPS (CS domain / IMSI) services, even though the EPS attach result IE literally indicates 'combined EPS/IMSI attach' was requested. This scenario arises typically when the SGSN/MSC combined procedure towards the CS domain fails or is not supported, while the EPS attach itself succeeds.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.20.2, which network entity may include the IMEISV request information element?

options.A: The Serving GPRS Support Node (SGSN)
options.B: The Mobility Management Entity (MME)
options.C: The Home Subscriber Server (HSS)
options.D: The Packet Data Network Gateway (PGW)

results.evidence: The network may include the IMEISV request information element in the SECURITY MODE COMMAND message, in which case the UE shall include its IMEISV in the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message.

results.question: According to clause 6.4.4.5, what action does the MME take upon the fifth expiry of timer T3495 during the EPS bearer context deactivation procedure?

options.A: The MME shall resend the DEACTIVATE EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST and restart timer T3495.
options.B: The MME shall abort the procedure and deactivate the EPS bearer context locally without peer-to-peer ESM signalling.
options.C: The MME shall initiate a new PDN disconnect procedure.
options.D: The MME shall wait indefinitely for a response from the UE.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.4.5, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: The MME shall, on the fifth expiry of the timer T3495, release the EPS bearer context and the PDN connection, if the requested EPS bearer context to be deactivated was the last EPS bearer context of a PDN connection, locally without peer to peer NAS signalling. The network shall also locally deactivate the EPS bearer context or PDN connection when the maximum number of retransmissions has been reached.

results.question: When a collision occurs between a UE requested PDN disconnect procedure and an EPS bearer context deactivation, and the EPS bearer being deactivated is a dedicated bearer belonging to the PDN connection the UE wants to disconnect, what does the MME do?

options.A: The MME shall ignore the PDN DISCONNECT REQUEST and proceed only with the deactivation.
options.B: The MME shall proceed with both procedures.
options.C: The MME shall abort the deactivation procedure and proceed only with the PDN disconnect.
options.D: The MME shall reject the PDN DISCONNECT REQUEST with an appropriate cause.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.4.5, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: If the EPS bearer context deactivation is related to a dedicated bearer of the PDN connection being disconnected, the MME shall progress the network-initiated EPS bearer context deactivation procedure only and shall locally deactivate the PDN connection without peer to peer NAS signalling procedure when the dedicated bearer deactivation procedure is completed.

results.question: Upon the first expiry of timer T3495 during the EPS bearer context deactivation procedure, what is the correct sequence of MME actions?

options.A: Abort the procedure and deactivate the bearer locally.
options.B: Resend the DEACTIVATE EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST, reset and restart timer T3495.
options.C: Send a PDN DISCONNECT REQUEST to the UE.
options.D: Wait for a retransmission from the UE before taking any action.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.4.5, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.evidence: Upon the first expiry of timer T3495, the MME shall resend the DEACTIVATE EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message and shall reset and restart timer T3495.

results.question: What is the specific purpose of including the Location Area Identification IE as described in TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.1.3?

options.A: To inform the UE about neighboring cell measurements
options.B: To assign a new location area identification to a UE
options.C: To confirm the UE's current routing area
options.D: To provide the UE with emergency service parameters

results.evidence: In TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.1.3 (ATTACH ACCEPT message, EMM procedures), the Location Area Identification (LAI) IE is included by the network to provide the UE with the Location Area Identity associated with the SGs/CS domain (MSC/VLR) when the EPS attach was performed as a combined EPS/IMSI attach. Its specific purpose is to inform the UE of the location area in which it is now registered for CS domain services, enabling proper operation of CS fallback (CSFB) and SMS-over-SGs procedures, and to allow the UE to detect a location area change requiring a subsequent combined tracking area/location area update.

results.question: What action is taken regarding the Location Area Identification IE during the procedure mentioned in TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.1.3?

options.A: It is used to validate the UE's previous location area
options.B: It is included to assign a new location area identification to the UE
options.C: It is removed to clear the UE's location context
options.D: It is compared with the UE's stored LAI for consistency

results.evidence: In TS 24.301 clause 8.2.1.3 (part of the ATTACH ACCEPT message definition/content description), the Location Area Identification IE is treated as a conditional/optional information element. The network includes the Location Area Identification IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT message only when the attach procedure being accepted is a combined EPS/IMSI attach (i.e., when the MME also performs a combined attach with the MSC/VLR via the SGs interface). In this case, the MME derives the Location Area Identification from the corresponding Tracking Area Identity and CS fallback mapping information, and includes it so that the UE can use it for subsequent CS-domain-related procedures (e.g., periodic LAU suppression). If the attach is EPS-only (not combined), the Location Area Identification IE is not included, and the UE shall not use or store an LAI from this message.

results.question: When a combined attach request is rejected by the network for both EPS and non-EPS services, and the failure is due to operator determined barring with a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST included, what message combination and EMM cause value should the MME use?

options.A: ATTACH REJECT with EMM cause #15 and PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT in ESM container
options.B: ATTACH REJECT with EMM cause #19 combined with PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT in ESM container
options.C: ATTACH REJECT with EMM cause #42 only, without ESM container
options.D: ATTACH REJECT with EMM cause #11 and separate PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.3.5, Combined attach not accepted by the network
results.evidence: If both EPS and non-EPS services are rejected due to operator determined barring, the MME shall combine ATTACH REJECT with EMM cause #8 'EPS services and non-EPS services not allowed' with PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT with ESM cause #8 'operator determined barring', and shall not activate any EPS bearer context.

results.question: Under what specific condition should the MME send an ATTACH REJECT with EMM cause #15 "No suitable cells in tracking area" when rejecting a combined attach?

options.A: When the rejection is due to NAS level mobility management congestion control
options.B: When the PDN connectivity reject is due to ESM cause #29 subject to operator policies
options.C: When the UE does not support EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection
options.D: When the network experiences severe failure (EMM cause #42)

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.3.5, Combined attach not accepted by the network
results.evidence: The MME shall reject the combined EPS/IMSI attach with EMM cause #15 'No suitable cells in tracking area' if the MS is located in a tracking area that is not suitable for the requested combined attach, specifically when the network does not support CS fallback or SMS-only services in the current tracking area for a non-EPS service (i.e., the tracking area is 'EPS services only' but the UE requested combined attach for both EPS and non-EPS services, or the tracking area does not support the requested non-EPS services), and no suitable cell can be found to provide the requested non-EPS services.

results.question: What is the required UE behavior regarding PLMN selection after receiving an ATTACH REJECT with EMM cause #42 (Severe network failure)?

options.A: Immediately attempt attach on the same PLMN+RAT
options.B: Not consider the PLMN+RAT combination as a candidate while an implementation-specific timer is running
options.C: Consider the PLMN+RAT combination as preferred for future selection
options.D: Perform cell reselection within the same tracking area

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.3.5, Combined attach not accepted by the network
results.evidence: Upon receiving ATTACH REJECT with EMM cause #42 'severe network failure', the UE shall perform a PLMN selection according to 3GPP TS 23.122, i.e., the UE shall consider that the current PLMN is not suitable for normal service and shall search for a new PLMN to select, rather than remaining camped on the current network or immediately retrying attach on the same cell/PLMN.

results.question: When a UE operating in single-registration mode receives an ATTACH REJECT for combined attach, what additional state changes must it perform?

options.A: Set GMM state to GMM-DEREGISTERED and delete TMSI
options.B: Set 5GMM state to 5GMM-DEREGISTERED and delete 5G-GUTI
options.C: Set both GMM and 5GMM states to DEREGISTERED
options.D: No additional state changes beyond EMM state

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.3.5, Combined attach not accepted by the network
results.evidence: If the ATTACH REJECT message is received for a combined attach and the UE operates in single-registration mode, the UE shall set the EPS update status to EU3 ROAMING NOT ALLOWED, shall delete any GUTI, TAI list, last visited registered TAI and eKSI, shall set the attach attempt counter to 5, and shall enter the state EMM-DEREGISTERED. Additionally, the UE shall set the update status to U3 ROAMING NOT ALLOWED and shall delete any TMSI, LAI and ciphering key sequence number, and shall enter the state GMM-DEREGISTERED or MM IDLE, as applicable, and shall set the EPS update status to EU3 ROAMING NOT ALLOWED.

results.question: What is the maximum number of possible entries in the UE's stored equivalent PLMNs list as specified in TS 24.301 Clause 5.3.4?
results.evidence: The UE shall store the equivalent PLMN list as provided by the network, up to a maximum of 16 entries, replacing any previously stored list.

results.question: Under which condition must the UE delete its stored equivalent PLMNs list according to TS 24.301 Clause 5.3.4?

options.A: When the UE performs a cell reselection
options.B: When the UE is switched off
options.C: When the USIM is removed
options.D: When the UE enters a new tracking area

results.evidence: The UE shall delete the stored list of equivalent PLMNs, if any, when: a) the UE is switched off; b) the UICC containing the USIM is removed; c) the attach procedure or tracking area updating procedure is not successful (e.g., the network rejects the attach or tracking area updating request or the procedure fails due to timer expiry after the maximum number of retries); or d) an attach procedure or tracking area updating procedure is completed successfully and the network does not include an Equivalent PLMNs information element in the ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message.

results.question: Which network layers use the same equivalent PLMNs list stored by the UE as specified in TS 24.301 Clause 5.3.4?

options.A: 5GMM and EMM only
options.B: EMM and GMM only
options.C: 5GMM, EMM, GMM and MM
options.D: MM and GMM only

results.evidence: The UE shall store the equivalent PLMN list as provided by the network, and both the Access Stratum (AS) and Non-Access Stratum (NAS) shall use this same list of equivalent PLMNs.

results.question: What action does the network take immediately upon receiving an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message?

options.A: It starts timer T3460 and checks the correctness of RES
options.B: It stops timer T3460 and checks the correctness of RES
options.C: It sends an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST with a new eKSI value
options.D: It renegotiates with HSS/AuC to obtain new authentication parameters

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.4, Authentication completion by the network
results.evidence: Upon receipt of an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message, the network stops timer T3460.

results.question: When the network initiates a new authentication procedure after successful completion, what requirement applies regarding the eKSI value in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message?

options.A: It must include the same eKSI value stored in the EPS security context
options.B: It must not include any eKSI value
options.C: It must include a different eKSI value than the one stored
options.D: It may include either the same or a different eKSI value

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.4, Authentication completion by the network
results.evidence: If the network initiates a new authentication procedure after having successfully completed a previous one, the network shall include an eKSI value in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message that differs from the eKSI value included in the previous AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message.

results.question: In the EMM-REGISTERED state, how shall the UE determine its behavior?

options.A: According to the radio access technology (RAT) in use
options.B: According to the network operator's policy settings
options.C: According to the substate as explained in clause 5.2.3.2
options.D: According to the UE's capability class

results.evidence: In state EMM-REGISTERED the UE shall behave as described in the following, depending on the specific EMM substate: EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE, EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE, EMM-REGISTERED.LIMITED-SERVICE, EMM-REGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH, EMM-REGISTERED.UPDATE-NEEDED, EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE, EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM, or EMM-REGISTERED.IMSI-DETACH-INITIATED. The UE behaviour in the EMM-REGISTERED state depends on the EMM substate and the applicable access technology and network conditions, and specific UE actions (e.g. cell selection, tracking area updating, service request, or paging response) are determined according to the substate the UE is currently in.

results.question: Under what condition is the Extended protocol configuration options IE included in a message according to clause 8.3.12.6?

options.A: When the UE wishes to transmit protocol data to the network
options.B: When the network wishes to transmit protocol data to the UE and extended PCO is supported end-to-end
options.C: When any protocol configuration needs to be updated, regardless of support
options.D: When the PDN connection is being established for the first time

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.12.6, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The Extended protocol configuration options IE is included in the message only if the network or the UE needs to transfer protocol configuration options information whose length exceeds the maximum length that can be carried by the Protocol configuration options IE, i.e., it is used to convey protocol configuration options data that cannot be accommodated within the standard PCO IE due to length constraints.

results.question: What type of data does clause 8.3.12.6 specify can be transmitted using the Extended protocol configuration options IE?

options.A: Only user plane data packets
options.B: Only authentication vectors and security keys
options.C: Protocol data such as configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events
options.D: Only handover-related measurement reports

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.12.6, Extended protocol configuration options
results.evidence: The purpose of the Extended protocol configuration options information element is to transfer external network protocol options associated with a PDN connection and/or containers for specific protocols, and/or additional parameters associated with SMS transfer via NAS, in cases where the data to be transferred exceeds the 253‑octet length limitation of the (non‑extended) Protocol configuration options IE.

results.question: In which scenario for a combined tracking area updating procedure does TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.26.14 specify that the network may include the 'Additional update result' IE?

options.A: When the procedure was successful for EPS services and 'SMS only'
options.B: When the procedure was successful for non-EPS services and 'SMS only'
options.C: When the procedure was partially successful for EPS services
options.D: When the procedure was initiated for emergency services

results.evidence: If the UE has set the SMS availability indicator to indicate that SMS over NAS is not available in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message, and the UE has requested combined attach or combined tracking area updating for SMS only (i.e. 'SMS only' EPS update type), the network may include the Additional update result IE set to 'SMS only, no CS fallback or packet services via S1' or 'SMS only' in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message to indicate that only SMS service is available over the current TA/RAT.

results.question: For a normal tracking area updating procedure requested for CIoT EPS optimizations, when may the network include the 'Additional update result' IE per TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.26.14?

options.A: When the procedure was successful for EPS services and non-EPS services
options.B: When the procedure was successful for EPS services and 'SMS only'
options.C: When the procedure was successful for non-EPS services only
options.D: When the procedure was successful for 'SMS only'

results.evidence: The network shall include the Additional update result IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message if the UE included the Additional update type IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message indicating support for control plane CIoT EPS optimization, and the network supports header compression for control plane CIoT EPS optimization; in this case, the network shall set the value to indicate 'header compression for control plane CIoT EPS optimization supported' or otherwise as appropriate to reflect the negotiated CIoT EPS optimization functionality (e.g., whether the network supports the requested optimization).

results.question: What is a common condition for including the 'Additional update result' IE in both combined TAU and normal TAU for CIoT EPS optimizations according to TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.26.14?

options.A: Success for EPS services and non-EPS services
options.B: Success for EPS services and 'SMS only'
options.C: Success for non-EPS services only
options.D: Partial success for EPS services

results.evidence: The Additional update result IE shall be included in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message if the requested type of network behaviour is 'PDN connectivity with EPS/CIoT optimizations' or the network is applying EPS/CIoT optimizations, and shall be included both for the case of combined tracking area updating and for the case of normal tracking area updating, in order to indicate to the UE the network's support of CIoT EPS optimizations (e.g. header compression, control plane CIoT EPS optimization) that the network is willing to apply.

results.question: Which combination of factors triggers the mandatory inclusion of the GPRS ciphering key sequence number IE?

options.A: EMM-CONNECTED mode and TIN indicating 'RAT-related TMSI'
options.B: EMM-IDLE mode, inter-system change from A/Gb or Iu mode to S1 mode, and TIN indicating 'P-TMSI'
options.C: Any inter-system change while the UE is in EMM-IDLE mode
options.D: S1 mode to Iu mode change with TIN indicating 'P-TMSI'

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.3, GPRS ciphering key sequence number
results.evidence: The GPRS ciphering key sequence number IE shall be included in the ROUTING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message if the TIN indicates 'P-TMSI' or if the routing area update request is sent as a response to paging with IMSI, and the UE is operating in Iu mode or A/Gb mode and has a valid GPRS ciphering key sequence number, so that the network can use it to avoid a new authentication procedure.

results.question: What does the TIN need to indicate to require inclusion of the GPRS ciphering key sequence number IE during an A/Gb or Iu mode to S1 mode inter-system change in EMM-IDLE mode?

options.A: GUTI
options.B: RAT-related TMSI
options.C: P-TMSI
options.D: No specific TIN value is required

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.3, GPRS ciphering key sequence number
results.evidence: The GPRS ciphering key sequence number IE shall be included if the TIN indicates 'P-TMSI'.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.17.3, what is the primary purpose of the NBIFOM container information element?

options.A: To manage UE power saving functions during mobility
options.B: To transfer information associated with network-based IP flow mobility
options.C: To establish security parameters for NAS signaling
options.D: To configure UE measurement reporting for handover

results.evidence: The purpose of the NBIFOM container information element is to transfer NBIFOM related parameters between the UE and the network in a transparent container, e.g. when the PDN connection uses Network-Based IP Flow Mobility (NBIFOM), as specified in 3GPP TS 24.161.

results.question: Which 3GPP specification is referenced in TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.17.3 for details about network-based IP flow mobility?

options.A: 3GPP TS 24.161
options.B: 3GPP TS 23.401
options.C: 3GPP TS 36.331
options.D: 3GPP TS 33.401

results.evidence: TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.17.3 states that for further details on network-based IP flow mobility, see 3GPP TS 23.261.

results.question: Based on TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.17.3, the NBIFOM container is used for information transfer related to:

options.A: Network-based access point name selection
options.B: Network-based IP flow mobility
options.C: Network-based bearer establishment
options.D: Network-based session management

results.evidence: The NBIFOM container information element is used to transfer NBIFOM (Network-Based IP Flow Mobility) related parameters between the UE and the network. It carries information such as the NBIFOM mode (UE-initiated or network-initiated), NBIFOM capability indication, and routing rules associated with IP flow mobility across multiple access networks during PDN connectivity establishment and modification procedures.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.20.6, what is the primary purpose of the NBIFOM container information element?

options.A: To transfer information associated with network-based IP flow mobility
options.B: To establish a new PDN connection for IP flow mobility
options.C: To manage handover procedures between 3GPP and non-3GPP access
options.D: To encapsulate QoS parameters for individual IP flows

results.evidence: The NBIFOM container information element is used to convey NBIFOM (Network-Based IP Flow Mobility) related parameters, such as NBIFOM mode, routing rules, and RAT (Radio Access Technology) usage information, between the UE and the network within ESM signalling messages, in order to negotiate and manage the establishment, modification and control of IP flow mobility for a PDN connection that has multiple accesses (e.g., 3GPP and non-3GPP).

results.question: Which 3GPP specification is referenced in TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.20.6 for details on network-based IP flow mobility?

options.A: 3GPP TS 24.161
options.B: 3GPP TS 23.401
options.C: 3GPP TS 24.302
options.D: 3GPP TS 29.274

results.evidence: TS 23.261 specifies the details of network-based IP flow mobility.

results.question: Based on TS 24.301 Clause 8.3.20.6, the NBIFOM container is used to transfer information for which specific functionality?

options.A: Network-based IP flow mobility
options.B: UE-based IP flow mobility
options.C: Access network discovery and selection
options.D: Traffic steering across multiple PDN connections

results.evidence: The NBIFOM container information element is used to transfer information related to network-based IP flow mobility (NBIFOM), as specified in 3GPP TS 24.161.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the Traffic flow aggregate description information element according to TS 24.301 clause 9.9.4.15?

options.A: To specify security parameters for EPS bearer contexts
options.B: To define the aggregate of one or more packet filters and their related parameters and operations
options.C: To establish the QoS parameters for voice over LTE calls
options.D: To manage handover procedures between 3G and 4G networks

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 9.9.4.15, Traffic flow aggregate description
results.evidence: The Traffic flow aggregate description information element is used by the network and the UE to specify a set of packet filters that identify a traffic flow aggregate, so that user data sent via the control plane (using the ESM DATA TRANSPORT message, e.g., for Control Plane CIoT EPS Optimization) can be associated with (i.e., mapped to) the correct EPS bearer context, thereby determining how the data should be handled by ESM.

results.question: Which entity applies the uplink packet filters defined in a traffic flow aggregate description?

options.A: The network (eNodeB)
options.B: The UE (User Equipment)
options.C: The MME (Mobility Management Entity)
options.D: The PGW (Packet Data Network Gateway)

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 9.9.4.15, Traffic flow aggregate description
results.evidence: The UE shall apply the uplink packet filters of the traffic flow aggregate description in the same way as it applies the uplink packet filters of a traffic flow template, i.e. the UE uses the uplink packet filters to determine the mapping of uplink packets to the EPS bearer context.

results.question: Under what condition is the Protocol configuration options IE included in a message according to clause 8.3.4.2?

options.A: When the network wishes to transmit protocol data to the UE
options.B: When the UE wishes to transmit protocol data to the network and extended protocol configuration options is not supported end-to-end
options.C: When the UE establishes any PDN connection regardless of support
options.D: When the network supports extended protocol configuration options for the session

results.evidence: The protocol configuration options IE is included if the UE requests to obtain, e.g., PCOs or PCSCF address, or if the network needs to send protocol configuration options to the UE, e.g., when the UE has included this IE in the corresponding request message and the network has protocol configuration options to send to the UE.

results.question: What type of data does clause 8.3.4.2 specify the UE may transmit using the Protocol configuration options IE?

options.A: Only authentication parameters
options.B: Only error codes
options.C: Protocol data such as configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events
options.D: Exclusively session management commands

results.evidence: In clause 8.3.4.2 (Protocol configuration options) of 3GPP TS 24.301, it is specified that the UE may use the Protocol configuration options (PCO) information element to transmit configuration and application‑level parameters that are not interpreted by the EPS mobility/session management entities but are transferred transparently between the UE and the PDN GW (or the network entity handling the PDN connection). This includes, for example, requests for P‑CSCF IPv4/IPv6 server address(es), DNS server IPv4/IPv6 address(es), MTU size requests, IM CN Subsystem Signalling Flag, and other vendor‑ or application‑specific configuration data.

results.question: What does clause 8.3.4.2 indicate about the relationship between Protocol configuration options and extended protocol configuration options?

options.A: They are always used together in every message
options.B: Protocol configuration options is used when extended protocol configuration options is not supported end-to-end
options.C: Extended protocol configuration options replaces Protocol configuration options in all cases
options.D: Protocol configuration options is only for network-to-UE data transfer

results.evidence: The Protocol configuration options information element and the Extended protocol configuration options information element shall not be present simultaneously in the ATTACH ACCEPT message. If both are received, the UE shall use the Extended protocol configuration options information element and shall ignore the Protocol configuration options information element.

results.question: How should a UE interpret the absence of the Network policy IE as specified in TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.26.22?

options.A: As an error condition requiring re-transmission
options.B: As receipt of an IE with all bits of the value part coded as zero
options.C: That no network policies are applicable to this UE
options.D: That the network policy remains unchanged from previous configuration

results.evidence: If the Network policy IE is not included in the ATTACH ACCEPT/TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, the UE shall interpret this absence as the network not providing any specific network policy indication (e.g. no restriction on NAS signalling low priority, no indication for congestion control handling). In this case, the UE shall behave according to the default UE behaviour applicable in the absence of network‑provided policy information, i.e. it shall not apply any network‑policy‑based restriction and shall continue to operate with its locally configured or previously received policy settings, if any, until a Network policy IE is subsequently received.

results.question: Based on TS 24.301 Clause 8.2.26.22, what is the UE's required action when the Network policy IE is not included?

options.A: Ignore any previously received network policies
options.B: Assume default network policy values defined in UE implementation
options.C: Interpret as receiving the IE with all value bits coded as zero
options.D: Send a request to the network for policy information

results.evidence: If the Network policy IE is not included, the UE shall consider that the network does not support control plane CIoT 5GS optimization or that no network policy information is provided, and the UE shall use the default behaviour applicable in the absence of this information.

results.question: What action must the UE take regarding the TMSI status IE in the ATTACH REQUEST message if it has no valid TMSI stored?

options.A: It shall omit the TMSI status IE entirely.
options.B: It shall include the TMSI status IE.
options.C: It shall include the TMSI based NRI container IE instead.
options.D: It shall set the TMSI status IE to indicate 'TMSI invalid'.

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.3.2, Combined attach procedure initiation
results.evidence: If the UE has no valid TMSI available, the UE shall include the TMSI status IE in the ATTACH REQUEST message, with the TMSI status information element set to indicate 'no valid TMSI available'.

results.question: When initiating a combined attach procedure for EPS services and 'SMS only', how must the UE indicate this in the ATTACH REQUEST message?

options.A: By setting the Attach type IE to 'SMS only'
options.B: By including the 'SMS only' indicator in the EPS attach type IE
options.C: By indicating 'SMS only' in the Additional update type IE
options.D: By setting the Session management type IE to 'SMS only'

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.3.2, Combined attach procedure initiation
results.evidence: In order to request a combined attach for EPS services and 'SMS only', the UE shall set the EPS attach type IE to 'combined EPS/IMSI attach' in the ATTACH REQUEST message, and shall not include any bearer(s) for user data other than the default EPS bearer context (i.e. it shall not include the ESM information for PDN connectivity setup that would activate additional dedicated bearers), while additionally including the necessary MS network capability, mobile station classmark, and DRX parameter IEs so that the network can determine that only SMS transport over NAS is being requested. The UE shall further indicate its support for 'SMS only' by not including any PDN connectivity request that would establish a default bearer used for user plane services, and shall set the EPS attach result requested to be consistent with 'combined EPS/IMSI attach for SMS only' as defined in the EPS attach type information element in clause 9.9.3.11 of 3GPP TS 24.301.

results.question: When the MME includes a new GUTI in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, what action must it take regarding timer T3450?

options.A: It shall stop timer T3450 if it is running
options.B: It shall start timer T3450
options.C: It shall reset timer T3450 to its initial value
options.D: No timer action is required when including GUTI

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.4, Normal and periodic tracking area updating procedure accepted by the network
results.evidence: If the tracking area updating procedure is not due to handover, the MME shall include a new GUTI in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message; if a new GUTI is included, the MME shall start timer T3450.

results.question: What restriction applies when the MME assigns a TAI list in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message?

options.A: The TAI list must contain at least three tracking areas
options.B: The TAI list cannot contain both NB-S1 mode and WB-S1 mode tracking areas
options.C: The TAI list must be identical to the UE's previously stored TAI list
options.D: The TAI list can only contain tracking areas from the current PLMN

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.4, Normal and periodic tracking area updating procedure accepted by the network
results.evidence: When the MME assigns a TAI list to the UE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, all TAIs contained in that TAI list shall belong to the same PLMN (i.e., have the same MCC and MNC), and the list shall not contain TAIs belonging to different PLMNs. Additionally, the TAI list can contain a maximum of 16 TAIs.

results.question: When a UE receives a Forbidden TAI(s) IE for 'forbidden tracking areas for roaming' in TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT, and the TAI(s) is not already in that list, what must the UE do?

options.A: Ignore the IE since it only applies during initial registration
options.B: Store the TAI(s) into the list and remove it from the stored TAI list if present
options.C: Store the TAI(s) but keep it in the stored TAI list for fallback purposes
options.D: Immediately initiate a detach procedure

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.4, Normal and periodic tracking area updating procedure accepted by the network
results.evidence: If the tracking area updating procedure is not initiated due to inter-system change and the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message contains a Forbidden TAI(s) IE for 'forbidden tracking areas for roaming', the UE shall, if the TAI(s) is not already in the stored list, add the TAI(s) to the stored list of 'forbidden tracking areas for roaming'.

results.question: What must the MME do with UE network capability information received in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message?

options.A: Store only the first octet of each capability IE
options.B: Store all octets received, up to the maximum length defined for each IE
options.C: Forward it immediately to the HSS for verification
options.D: Ignore it unless the UE is in emergency services mode

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.4, Normal and periodic tracking area updating procedure accepted by the network
results.evidence: The MME shall store the UE network capability and MS network capability IEs, if received, as part of the EMM context of the UE, and shall consider these IEs, together with the UE additional security capability, to determine the security capabilities of the UE for the selection of NAS and AS security algorithms (see subclause 9.9.3.34, 9.9.3.20 and 9.9.3.12B).

results.question: When the network activates APN-based congestion control, which of the following session management requests may still be accepted from UEs?

options.A: PDN connectivity requests for new non-emergency connections
options.B: Bearer resource modification requests
options.C: PDN disconnection requests for emergency connections
options.D: ESM information requests for congested APNs

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.5, Handling of APN based congestion control
results.evidence: When APN based congestion control is active for an APN, the network shall reject session management requests from the UE for that APN, except that the network shall not reject a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message with the request type set to 'emergency', a BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REQUEST or BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST message associated with a PDN connection established for emergency bearer services, or a PDN DISCONNECT REQUEST message. Such requests for emergency bearer services shall always be accepted regardless of APN based congestion control.

results.question: What happens when a UE does not provide an APN for a non-emergency PDN connection and APN-based congestion control is needed?

options.A: The MME rejects the request with cause #27 'missing or unknown APN'
options.B: The MME uses the APN from the UE's default PDN connection
options.C: The MME uses the APN which is used in PDN GW selection procedure as congested APN
options.D: The MME assigns a temporary APN for congestion control purposes

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.5, Handling of APN based congestion control
results.evidence: If the UE does not provide an APN when requesting a PDN connection for other than emergency bearer services, and the network needs to apply APN based congestion control for that request, the MME or SGSN shall determine the APN to be used for congestion control purposes as the default APN indicated in the subscription data received from the HSS (i.e., the APN that would have been selected by the network for that UE had the UE not experienced congestion). The request is then handled as if it were associated with that (subscribed) default APN for the purpose of applying APN based congestion control, mobility management congestion control being applied instead if this determination cannot be made.

results.question: Which of the following procedures is a UE allowed to initiate when timer T3396 for an APN is running or deactivated?

options.A: Initiate a new PDN connectivity request for the same APN
options.B: Initiate bearer resource modification to release bearer resources for that APN

options.D: Initiate a PDN connectivity request for a different non-emergency APN

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.5, Handling of APN based congestion control
results.evidence: If timer T3396 is running or the network indicates that the timer is deactivated for the APN, the UE shall not send a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message for that APN. results.question: During an established EMM context, how many EMM INFORMATION messages can the network send to the UE, as specified in clause 5.4.5.2?

options.A: Exactly one
options.B: None or exactly one

options.D: A fixed number defined by network policy

results.question: If the network sends multiple EMM INFORMATION messages to the UE during an established EMM context, what does clause 5.4.5.2 specify about their content?

options.A: All messages must have identical content for consistency
options.B: The messages need not have the same content

results.evidence: The EMM INFORMATION message is sent by the network at any time during the EMM context established, and if the network sends multiple EMM INFORMATION messages during the EMM context established, then the last EMM INFORMATION message received by the UE shall take precedence over any previously received EMM INFORMATION message content.

results.question: Based on clause 5.4.5.2, what does the EMM information procedure consist of?

options.A: An EMM INFORMATION request from the UE and a response from the network

This message may be sent to the UE by the network at any time during an EMM-REGISTERED state, and is used to transfer network name, time zone, and universal time and local time information from the network to the UE.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 clause 7.5.1, when a UE receives a message with a syntactically incorrect mandatory IE, and the message is NOT one of those listed in clause 7.5.3 items a, b, c, or d, what action must the UE take?

options.D: Return a status message with cause #97 'message type non-existent or not implemented'

If, after this, the message contains a syntax error according to subclause 7.5.2, the UE shall treat it as specified for that erroneous message in subclause 7.5.2.

results.question: Which of the following error conditions, when diagnosed by the UE upon receipt of a message, triggers the procedures specified in clause 7.5.1?

options.A: A 'protocol error' in an optional IE
options.B: A 'missing mandatory IE' error
options.C: A 'conditional IE error' in a non-mandatory IE
options.D: An 'unexpected message' error for a known message type

results.evidence: The UE shall diagnose that a message is semantically incorrect if the message is defined for the network state and contains information elements which, though correctly coded, contain information that is inconsistent with the current state of the UE, i.e. the message is in contradiction to the protocol state or context (e.g. contains an invalid combination of information elements or unacceptable values), and this diagnosis of a semantically incorrect EPS mobility management message shall trigger the specific error handling procedures described in clause 7.5.1.

results.question: In which scenario would the network NOT include the T3448 value IE based on the specified clause?

options.A: When congestion control for user data via control plane is inactive, even if UE supports T3448

results.evidence: As specified in 3GPP TS 24.301 (e.g., subclauses 5.5.1.2.5, 5.5.1.3.5, 5.5.3.2.5/3.5 and 5.6.3.7 dealing with EMM common/attach/TAU/service reject procedures not accepted by the network due to congestion control), the network shall not include the T3448 value IE in the ATTACH REJECT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT or SERVICE REJECT message when the UE has not indicated support for the control plane CIoT EPS optimization (i.e., the UE is not using, or has not requested, the control plane CIoT EPS optimization). In such a case, only the T3346 value IE (back-off timer) is used for congestion control, since T3448 is applicable only to UEs operating with control plane CIoT EPS optimization.

results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 4.3.2.1, which of the following events can trigger a change in the UE mode of operation for a CS voice capable UE?

options.A: A change in the UE's usage setting
options.B: A change in the UE's battery level
options.C: A change in the UE's radio access technology preference
options.D: A change in the UE's international roaming status

results.question: What specific condition can cause a UE to transition from CS/PS mode 1 to PS mode 1, as noted in TS 24.301 Clause 4.3.2.1?

options.D: When the UE receives an SMS over IMS

results.question: For a CS voice capable UE, a change in which parameter defined in 3GPP TS 24.167 can trigger a change in UE mode of operation?

options.A: Voice domain preference for E-UTRAN
options.B: IMS registration status
options.C: Packet data protocol context
options.D: Access point name configuration

results.question: After transitioning to PS mode 1 due to 'CS domain not available', what event might cause the UE to transition back to CS/PS mode 1?

options.A: A change of PLMN which is not in the list of equivalent PLMNs
options.B: A change in the UE's IMS registration status
options.C: Receipt of an SMS over the CS domain
options.D: The UE's battery level dropping below 10%

results.evidence: TS 24.301, subclause 4.3.5.2 (Coordination between EPS services and non‑EPS services – network operation modes): 'If the UE has entered PS mode 1 of operation because the network indicated that the CS domain is not available (e.g. the EPS ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message included the EPS network feature support IE or additional update result IE with an indication that CS domain services are not available, or the combined attach/TAU procedure was rejected/only partially accepted for the CS domain), the UE shall revert to CS/PS mode 1 of operation as soon as it receives an indication that the CS domain has become available again. Such an indication is typically obtained when the UE performs a new combined EPS/IMSI attach or combined tracking area updating procedure (e.g. triggered by a tracking area/routing area change, cell reselection to a different PLMN or RAT, periodic TAU, or a lower layer/CS domain availability indication) and the network returns an EPS attach result/TAU result indicating that combined EPS/IMSI attach (or combined TAU) for both EPS and non‑EPS services was successful, i.e. no longer indicating that the CS domain is unavailable.'

results.question: Under what conditions shall a UE that supports CE mode B and operates in WB-S1 mode not using satellite E-UTRAN access apply the NAS timer values from tables 10.2.1 and 10.3.1 for WB-S1/CE mode?

options.A: When the UE's usage setting is set to 'voice centric' and enhanced coverage is not restricted.
options.B: When the UE's usage setting is not set to 'voice centric' AND (enhanced coverage is not restricted OR CE mode B is not restricted).

results.question: According to the clause, when is the calculated NAS timer value recalculated during a procedure?

options.A: It is recalculated periodically throughout the NAS procedure.
options.B: It is recalculated whenever the UE changes between CE mode A and CE mode B.
options.C: It is not recalculated until the NAS procedure is completed, restarted, or aborted.
options.D: It is recalculated after receiving each new NAS message from the network.

results.evidence: The calculated value of the timer is recalculated each time the timer is (re-)started during the procedure, i.e. not only when the timer is started for the first time, so that a new random value is used for every restart of the timer during that procedure.

results.question: Besides a missing network response, what other reason can trigger entry into EMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-ATTACH?

options.A: UE powering down normally
options.B: Network sending an explicit detach command
options.C: Circumstances described in specific referenced clauses
options.D: Successful authentication procedure completion

results.question: A UE operating in PS mode 1 has its voice domain preference for E-UTRAN changed from 'IMS PS voice only' to 'CS voice preferred, IMS PS Voice as secondary'. According to TS 24.301 clause 4.3.2.3, what procedure must the UE execute?

options.B: Disable the E-UTRA capability immediately

results.question: A UE operating in CS/PS mode 2 changes its voice domain preference for E-UTRAN from any configuration to 'IMS PS voice only'. The UE is configured to prefer SMS over IP networks and is available for voice calls in the IMS. What action must the UE take?

options.C: Perform a combined tracking area update with IMSI attach
options.D: Re-enable the E-UTRA capability if it was disabled

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.3.2.3, Change of voice domain preference for E-UTRAN
results.evidence: If the UE is configured for 'SMS over IP networks' and the value part of Voice domain preference for E-UTRAN indicates 'IMS PS voice only' or the UE is not configured for 'SMS over NAS' and the value part of Voice domain preference for E-UTRAN indicates 'IMS PS voice only', 'IMS PS voice preferred, CS voice as secondary' or 'CS voice preferred, IMS PS voice as secondary', and if the UE is available for voice calls in the IMS, then upon a change of the value part of the Voice domain preference for E-UTRAN parameter to 'IMS PS voice only', the UE shall perform a tracking area updating procedure to indicate its SMS availability, if 'SMS over IP' is supported and the UE is not already indicating SMS availability.

results.question: A UE is operating in CS/PS mode 1. Its voice domain preference for E-UTRAN changes from any configuration to 'CS voice only'. options.C: Perform a combined tracking area update with IMSI attach
options.D: Re-enable the E-UTRA capability immediately

results.evidence: If the UE is configured for CS/PS mode 1 or CS/PS mode 2 of operation, and the voice domain preference for E-UTRAN has changed from any value to 'CS Voice only', the UE shall initiate a tracking area updating procedure indicating 'SMS only' or 'combined TA/LA updating with IMSI attach' as appropriate, if the UE received a 'CS fallback not preferred' or 'SMS only' indication from the network in the last ATTACH ACCEPT message or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message.

results.question: A UE's voice domain preference for E-UTRAN changes from 'CS voice only' to another configuration. options.B: Re-enable the E-UTRA capability immediately, regardless of the RRC connection
options.C: Delay re-enabling the E-UTRA capability until the RRC connection is released
options.D: Perform a combined tracking area update before taking any action on E-UTRA capability

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.3.2.3, Change of voice domain preference for E-UTRAN
results.evidence: If the UE's voice domain preference for E-UTRAN changes from 'CS Voice only' and the UE's E-UTRA capability was disabled due to a change of the UE's usage setting or the voice domain preference for E-UTRAN, the UE shall set the UE's E-UTRA capability to enabled. results.question: According to TS 24.301 Clause 6.5.1.4A, what action must a UE take when the maximum number of active EPS bearer contexts is reached and upper layers request connectivity to a new PDN?

options.A: Send a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message immediately with a special flag
options.B: Initiate a tracking area update procedure before sending any request
options.C: Not send a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message unless an active EPS bearer is deactivated
options.D: Send a modified PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST that bypasses the bearer limit check

results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.1.4A, Handling the maximum number of active EPS bearer contexts
results.evidence: If the UE receives a request from upper layers for PDP context activation for connectivity to a PDN, or for emergency bearer services, and the UE has reached the maximum number of active EPS bearer contexts, the UE shall initiate the deactivation of an existing PDN connection, e.g. one that was established for the purpose of connecting to that PDN, in order to be able to activate the requested new PDN connection or to establish emergency bearer services.
